item.title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
item.description: NEW DELHI: Steffan Jones, former high-performance coach at Rajasthan Royals (RR), will join Mumbai Indians (MI) as a bowling consultant for their development program, TimesofIndia.com has learnt. The 52-year-old will work with MI's development squad alongside Zubin Bharucha, who has joined the five-time champions as director of performance, earlier this year. Jones, who also served as Rajasthan Royals' fast-bowling coach during the 2019 edition of the IPL, was later brought back by the franchise as its high-performance fast-bowling coach ahead of IPL 2022. It is also learnt that Bharucha and Jones have a specific role: to work with Indian players during the ongoing domestic season. Jones, who played first-class cricket in the English county circuit between 1997 and 2011, recently worked with India all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy. The Welshman helped the youngster improve his bowling speed. Reddy, who used to bowl in the mid-120s, is now consistently clocking the mid-130s. Earlier on Saturday, MI roped in Kieron Pollard as their head coach, replacing Mahela Jayawardene. The franchise is likely to take the big call on captaincy and movement is expected on Hardik Pandya trade in the coming weeks.

item.title: American Paula Moltzan wins Alpine skiing's World Cup opener, her first career win
item.description: Moltzan, 32, had reached 10 podiums but never won a World Cup race before Saturday. She was the giant slalom bronze medalist at the 2025 World Championships.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham Backs Angel Reese’s Demand: “We Need to Get Her the D*** Ball”
item.description: Sophie Cunningham expected a tight WNBA Finals. Instead, she watched the Atlanta Dream overwhelm the Golden State Valkyries. “I am shocked by how much Atlanta is winning by,” the Indiana Fever guard said on the latest episode of her podcast, “No Hesitation.” “They’re not just winning, they are kicking complete a**.” Cunningham broke down the first three games of the best-of-seven series with co-host Drew Hanlen, a basketball skills trainer. Atlanta leads two games to one entering Game 4 on Saturday afternoon at State Farm Arena, after Golden State won the opener and the Dream answered with 14- and 26-point wins. The show debuted Sept. 10 on The Volume, replacing Cunningham’s previous podcast, “Show Me Something,” and focusing on film study and strategy. On the first episode, she said she felt no show offered “real, honest truth about basketball and strictly basketball.” “I knew this series was not going to be a skunking type situation. I knew it was going to go back and forth,” Cunningham said. Cunningham, 30, is coming off her eighth WNBA season, which she played on a one-year deal after tearing her right MCL in August 2025. item.content:encoded: Sophie Cunningham expected a tight WNBA Finals. Instead, she watched the Atlanta Dream overwhelm the Golden State Valkyries. “I am shocked by how much Atlanta is winning by,” the Indiana Fever guard said on the latest episode of her podcast, “No Hesitation.” “They’re not just winning, they are kicking complete a**.” Cunningham broke down the first three games of the best-of-seven series with co-host Drew Hanlen, a basketball skills trainer. Atlanta leads two games to one entering Game 4 on Saturday afternoon at State Farm Arena, after Golden State won the opener and the Dream answered with 14- and 26-point wins. The show debuted Sept. 10 on The Volume, replacing Cunningham’s previous podcast, “Show Me Something,” and focusing on film study and strategy. On the first episode, she said she felt no show offered “real, honest truth about basketball and strictly basketball.” “I knew this series was not going to be a skunking type situation. I knew it was going to go back and forth,” Cunningham said. Cunningham, 30, is coming off her eighth WNBA season, which she played on a one-year deal after tearing her right MCL in August 2025. She shot 43.2% from the 3-point range in 2025, third-best in the league. Her Fever were knocked out in the first round this year by the Las Vegas Aces; the defending champions, Golden State, then swept in the semifinals. Both Finals teams are chasing a first championship. The Valkyries reached the Finals in only their second season, and the Dream had never won a Finals game in three previous trips before this series. Slow and steady wins Game 1, then Atlanta hits the gas Golden State won the opener 68 to 64 at Chase Center on Oct. 17, led by 26 points from Gabby Williams. Atlanta went 2 for 19 from the field in the fourth quarter and did not score over the final 3 minutes, 12 seconds. Cunningham, who called Golden State the slowest team in the WNBA, said the Valkyries got exactly the game they wanted. “They want to control the pace. They want to slow down. They want to play half court defense and half court offense,” she said. “Game 1, they were definitely setting the tone with their pace, with their pressure and controlling that.” The answer, in her view, was obvious. “If you’re really any other team outside of Valkyries, you want to run on them,” Cunningham said. “You want that game pace to be absolutely high because that is not what they like to do.” Hanlen admitted Game 1 had him leaning Golden State. “After that first game, I was convinced that Golden State was going to kind of run through this series and Atlanta might sneak a game or two,” he said. Of Atlanta’s fourth-quarter shooting, he added, “Again, not a typo, not a misstep. Notice every shot is contested.” Still, he noted the Dream had a late 3-point attempt to win it. “Even though it looks like we got dominated, we still were right in the game,” he said, describing how a Dream fan might see it. Atlanta ran in Game 2. The Dream won 79 to 65 on Oct. 19 for the first Finals victory in franchise history, scoring 24 points off a season-high 19 Golden State turnovers. Angel Reese had 30 points and 16 rebounds, Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals, Allisha Gray scored 18, and Jordin Canada added 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds. Hanlen said the Dream won fast-break points 19 to 0. Game 3 moved from the Dream’s usual home at Gateway Center Arena, which seats about 3,500, to the Hawks’ State Farm Arena, which holds about 17,000, and sold out. Golden State did not make a field goal for the first 4 minutes, 53 seconds and lost 97 to 71. Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds as one of five Dream players in double figures, and Atlanta turned 17 turnovers into 22 points. Hanlen said the series has followed the keys he set out before it began: 3-point shooting, Atlanta’s top scorers, and the battle between full-court and half-court basketball. “The formula is kind of the formula,” he said. “My high school coach had a saying: toughest team wins. And that’s exactly what you’re seeing in this series.” Atlanta’s defense brings the bark and the bite For Cunningham, the series comes down to one thing, and it is not shooting. “Valkyries had one of the best defenses all season long and so did Atlanta,” she said. “What’s sticking out to me is Atlanta’s defense. It’s every single game of the series. Who can step it up even more? Who can be a dog even more? Who can bring that tenacity even more than they did the last game? And honestly, Atlanta has been doing that.” “We can do all these numbers. We can watch film, but whoever is kicking a** on defense is typically who’s going to win,” Cunningham said. “And I think Atlanta has been proving that point, too.” She said the pressure in Game 2 pushed Golden State into habits it had avoided all season, pointing to a turnover on a simple pass by Veronica Burton, whom she called one of the league’s best point guards. “The pressure of Atlanta’s defense was causing the Valkyries to do uncharacteristic things that they haven’t done all year,” Cunningham said. “You got to give Atlanta credit for raising their bar of defensive intensity and making them do stuff that they’re not comfortable with.” That aggression also explains the free throw gap in Game 2, when Atlanta attempted 35 free throws to Golden State’s 19 and drew complaints online, she said. “If you’re the aggressor and you’re kind of setting the tone, you kind of have the momentum, naturally, you’re going to get those calls more than the other team,” Cunningham said. Hanlen walked through the scheme behind it. “They’ve basically turned Golden State into an isolation team,” he said. “They’re not letting them drive and kick. They’re not helping out.” Atlanta now stays attached through Golden State’s ghost screens and starts its help defenders inside before sliding out to shooters, the same approach the hosts recommended before the series. “Are they listening to our podcast?” Hanlen joked. Describing Atlanta’s plan, he said, “We’re going to make them beat us with hard twos instead of the drive-and-kick dominoes that we saw them dominate with,” and he called it “a big, big compliment to their coaching staff and to their players.” Cunningham said the credit is shared. “Our coaches, no matter what team you’re on, they spend days on days on days watching film and trying to clip it to help us players be successful, but Atlanta’s actually executing it,” she said. “So, you got to give credit to both.” “They’re being freaking dogs right now on the defensive end, and they don’t care,” Cunningham said. “They’re playing with reckless abandonment and it’s working for them.” “Their players are playing, man,” she added. “They have peaked at the right d*** time.” Give Angel the ball, and nobody gets hurt The moment Cunningham and Hanlen agreed changed the series came early in Game 2. Reese repeatedly sealed her defender and raised her hand for the ball without getting it, then walked back on defense visibly frustrated and turned toward her bench. Some on social media called her a baby for it. Cunningham, known for her own fiery edge, made three points in Reese’s defense. First, she said, frustration comes with the stakes. “You could probably clip almost everybody in the WNBA, in the NBA, that has clips like this, the frustration clips,” Cunningham said. “That’s what you get when you’re playing at a high level, when you’re a competitor, especially when you’re trying to get a championship. This s*** is going to happen.” Second, she conceded the body language could have been better. “Absolutely,” Cunningham said. “And I think if she watches this back, I think she could have said the same thing.” Third, she said, sometimes a star has to demand it. “But sometimes you got to do it,” Cunningham said. “If your team’s not getting you the d*** ball, then if you see one of your star players getting frustrated … it’s like, oh, they’re not messing around. We need to get her

item.title: Moltzan upstages Shiffrin to win season-opening World Cup giant slalom
item.description: USA's Paula Moltzan en route to victory in the giant slalom in Soelden (Johann GRODER) Paula Moltzan upstaged feted US teammate Mikaela Shiffrin to win the season-opening women's World Cup giant slalom in Soelden on Saturday. World bronze medallist Moltzan, fifth fastest after the first of two legs on the Rettenbach slope in the Austrian resort, held her nerve on the second descent for a combined winning time of 2min 14.82sec. After 10 podiums in 13 World Cup seasons, it was the 32-year-old American's first-ever victory on the elite alpine skiing circuit. Italian-born Albanian Lara Colturi was second, just one-hundredth of a second off the American, with Germany's Emma Aicher rounding out the podium (+0.52sec). Shiffrin, seeking a record-stretching 111th victory on the World Cup circuit, finished seventh, 0.83sec off Moltzan's pace. Shiffrin had led Sweden's Sara Hector by 0.14sec in the first leg, with Switzerland's Camille Rast in third (+0.37). Austria's Julia Scheib, winner of last season's GS crystal globe and defending champion in Soelden, was the biggest casualty of the first run, sliding out high up the course. Come the second run, Poland's Maryna Gasienca-Daniel set the pace, clocking an electric 1:06.16, after finishing just 29th in the first leg. Italian Asja Zenere, running 15th, eventually snatched the lead away from the Pole, whose time down the second run remained the quickest of the field. Germany's Aicher, ninth quickest in the first descent, roared into first place as racing entered the business end of proceedings. - Foggy conditions - In partly cloudy, bone-chilling conditions, neither Norway's Mina Fuerst Holtmann nor Sweden's Estelle Alphand could improve on the aggregate time. But Colturi did, enjoying a 0.51sec advantage at the top of the leaderboard. Moltzan was next up and grabbed the lead by a hair's breadth over Colturi. All eyes then turned on the top four from the first leg. First into the startgate was Canada's Britt Richardson but an error-ridden run saw her finish well down the field. Swiss racer Rast failed to trouble the podium while Sweden's 2022 Olympic GS champion Hector paid the price for one mistake, finishing behind Moltzan, Colturi and Aicher. Only Shiffrin was left to come down the Rettenbach slope, and she kicked out of the hut with a 0.59sec lead. But in increasingly foggy conditions, Shiffrin failed to maintain that, sliding wide on one turn, a move that saw her eventually finish seventh. The men's World Cup gets under way on Sunday, with racers also tackling a giant slalom in Soelden. lp/ea

item.title: ‘More pro China than pro America’: Clay Travis says national anthem video is a ‘reflection of who LeBron James is’
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia 76ers’ newest addition, LeBron James, has quickly shown the deal was worth it as the team starts the NBA season 2-0. But on opening night Tuesday in New York, James was caught on camera visibly practicing his golf swing as the national anthem played, causing a media frenzy afterward. The video shared by ClutchPoints showed James swinging his arms as if practicing his golf stroke, then going through his shooting motion. The criticism came from all directions , with many painting James as a villain to America for not being engaged during “The Star-Spangled Banner.” That included the President of the United States. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country!” Trump posted on Truth Social, via TheWrap . “I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP.” Conservative sports commentator and Sports and State founder Clay Travis chimed in and didn’t hesitate to question James’ allegiance to the United States. “Zero percent chance LeBron would practice a golf swing during China’s national anthem. 0%,” Travis posted on X Thursday afternoon. Travis doubled down on his original message in another post , writing, “LeBron would never disrespect the Chinese national anthem like he did the American national anthem this week. LeBron hates the country that made him a billionaire. His brain is broken.” He then took to Fox News on Friday morning to rip James even further. “He respects China more than he respects the United States,” Travis said live on Fox News. “LeBron James is a billionaire, a billionaire with a ‘B’ because he is fortunate enough to be really good at sports. If anyone should be grateful and thankful for all of the sacrifices that have occurred to allow him to have the level of economic success playing a game, it should be LeBron James. This is insanely disrespectful; the president was right to call him out for this.” After Philly’s comeback win against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday, reporters approached James, eager to hear his response to Trump’s latest message. “Must (have been) a slow news day at the office, you know? Slow news day in the office,” James said after the game, via USA Today . After the video aired in studio, Travis pounced on the opportunity to land his closing jabs before being cut off. “Yeah, that’s the wrong answer,” Travis added. “He should have said, ‘I’m a moron; I apologize.’ He didn’t do it. It’s not a slow news day; it’s more a reflection of who LeBron James is, more pro-China than pro-America.” The post ‘More pro China than pro America’: Clay Travis says national anthem video is a ‘reflection of who LeBron James is’ appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: ‘You have no business classifying yourself as that’: Stephen A. Smith rips Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer after ‘great coach’ comments
item.description: Nov 23, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; A general view of a Dallas Cowboys helmet before the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys have started the 2026 season off 2-4 and are currently tied for second in the NFC East. Media vultures have hounded the Cowboys’ lackluster effort so far and won’t ease up anytime soon if head coach Brian Schottenheimer can’t turn his team around. During a recent episode of ESPN’s First Take , Stephen A. Smith did not hold back after he reacted to a recent clip of Schottenheimer proclaiming himself a “great coach” during a press conference. “I know what a great coach I am,” Schottenheimer said, via Clarence Hill of AllCity DLLS . “But at the same time, I’ve got strong shoulders.” The First Take crew attempted to hold back laughter early as they sensed Smith was gearing up for a classic rebuttal to the Cowboys’ head coach. “Respectfully, Brian Schottenheimer, you have no business classifying yourself as that,” Smith said on First Take . “That’s problem one, two, and three. He seems like a really nice man… His record as a head coach in the National Football League is 9-13-1. If that is his definition of great, there’s a whole bunch of people out here that are great that we haven’t been talking about. You just can’t say stuff like that. “Let me ask Brian Schottenheimer a rhetorical question. If your quarterback completed 41% of his passes, would you call him great? If your defense gave up 41 points a game, would you call them great? “If you were not the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys and somebody else was coaching them, and in the two years that they were coaching, one year they didn’t make the playoffs and another year they’re underachieving, two games under .500, with the most potent offense arguably in the sport.” Smith continued to bash the Cowboys coach with off-the-field analogies centered on his coaching record, but quickly pivoted to show his seriousness and discernment for the Cowboys organization. “This is about bare-bones facts,” Smith added. “What the hell are you doing with cameras rolling and the microphone hot, as a grown-ass man and a head coach of an NFL franchise four games under .500 in your career, and you actually uttered out of your mouth, ‘I know I’m a great coach.’ Come on, man…go out there and prove it.” The Cowboys look to face off against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 on Monday Night Football . The Cowboys need a win, and Schottenheimer will be looking to quiet critics and spectators who doubt his coaching. The post ‘You have no business classifying yourself as that’: Stephen A. Smith rips Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer after ‘great coach’ comments appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Jets vs. Dolphins: 3 key matchups to watch in Week 7
item.description: The New York Jets (2-4) will look to get back in the win column as they host the Miami Dolphins (0-5) at MetLife Stadium in Week 7. The Jets put together another good effort but were doomed by self-inflicted mistakes that cost them points as well as shoddy defense in the fourth quarter in their 26-19 loss to New England. Miami is in a full-blown rebuilding year under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. They are still looking for their first win but have been competitive over their last two games, including a near upset win over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. The Dolphins have won five of their last six against the Jets going back to 2023. Here are three key matchups in the Jets Week 7 matchup against the Miami Dolphins: Ollie Gordon II vs. The Jets Defensive Line The Jets rushing defense struggled last week, allowing 148 yards on the ground to the Patriots. Backup running back Corey Kiner, who led all New England running backs with 57 yards on the ground, had 42 yards on the final drive that resulted in a field goal and sealed the victory for the Patriots. The Jets as a team have allowed just over 123 yards on the ground this year, which ties them for 23rd in the league with Cincinnati. The Dolphins suffered a brutal blow to their rebuilding season when De'von Achane was lost for the season after suffering a torn ACL. Ollie Gordon II, Miami's sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft, has stepped in and ran the ball well in Achane’s absence, with three touchdowns, 188 yards rushing and an average of over seven yards per carry in his last two games. Miami’s offense isn’t really anything to be too scared of, but they have a strong running game which is ranked eighth overall as they average just over 126 yards on the ground per game. Couple that with the fact the Jets are not a great team against the run and Miami could have a key advantage in Sunday's game. If they can slow Gordon down on Sunday, it will put plenty of pressure on Malik Willis to make plays, something he has not been very good at this year. Garrett Wilson vs. Juju Brents I’ll never understand why the Jets media insist on creating this false narrative about Wilson’s unhappiness. Wilson leads the team with 48 targets, has three touchdowns on the year and averaging just under 12 yards a reception. Of course, he could be utilized more in the offense. item.content:encoded: The New York Jets (2-4) will look to get back in the win column as they host the Miami Dolphins (0-5) at MetLife Stadium in Week 7. The Jets put together another good effort but were doomed by self-inflicted mistakes that cost them points as well as shoddy defense in the fourth quarter in their 26-19 loss to New England. Miami is in a full-blown rebuilding year under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. They are still looking for their first win but have been competitive over their last two games, including a near upset win over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. The Dolphins have won five of their last six against the Jets going back to 2023. Here are three key matchups in the Jets Week 7 matchup against the Miami Dolphins: Ollie Gordon II vs. The Jets Defensive Line The Jets rushing defense struggled last week, allowing 148 yards on the ground to the Patriots. Backup running back Corey Kiner, who led all New England running backs with 57 yards on the ground, had 42 yards on the final drive that resulted in a field goal and sealed the victory for the Patriots. The Jets as a team have allowed just over 123 yards on the ground this year, which ties them for 23rd in the league with Cincinnati. The Dolphins suffered a brutal blow to their rebuilding season when De'von Achane was lost for the season after suffering a torn ACL. Ollie Gordon II, Miami's sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft, has stepped in and ran the ball well in Achane’s absence, with three touchdowns, 188 yards rushing and an average of over seven yards per carry in his last two games. Miami’s offense isn’t really anything to be too scared of, but they have a strong running game which is ranked eighth overall as they average just over 126 yards on the ground per game. Couple that with the fact the Jets are not a great team against the run and Miami could have a key advantage in Sunday's game. If they can slow Gordon down on Sunday, it will put plenty of pressure on Malik Willis to make plays, something he has not been very good at this year. Garrett Wilson vs. Juju Brents I’ll never understand why the Jets media insist on creating this false narrative about Wilson’s unhappiness. Wilson leads the team with 48 targets, has three touchdowns on the year and averaging just under 12 yards a reception. Of course, he could be utilized more in the offense. But, the same fan base and beat writers who said the Jets need more weapons are now frustrated that Wilson doesn't lead the team in targets each week. Will Jets Nation ever be satisfied? For Sunday, Wilson will most likely face off against Brents, who is a former second round pick of the Indianapolis Colts. He’s not a great cornerback, but he’s got size (6’3”, 198 lbs.) and has been good in coverage this year. Brents was excellent in Miami’s loss to Cincinnati in Week 5 with two tackles, four assists and one pass breakup, earning a PFF grade of 90.4 for that game. The Jets could have Adonai Mitchell back for Sunday, which should open up plenty of opportunities for Wilson to have a monster game. Frank Reich has to get his best playmaker the ball as the offense runs better when Wilson is heavily involved. David Bailey vs. Austin Jackson After Bailey’s breakout game against the Browns with 3 sacks in Week 5, the rookie was held in check by the Patriots offensive line, which is surprising as during that game, New England lost two starters, including Alijah Vera-Tucker. Bailey did have a forced fumble last week and while we know he’s not going to be a monster each and every game, it was a bit of a bad look that he couldn’t generate much pressure against New England’s backup offensive line. Jackson is a former first-round pick of the Dolphins and has been terrible this season. He ranks at the bottom of the league as a pass blocker, has allowed three sacks and 19 total pressures. He has a PFF Pass-Blocking grade of 41.2, ranking him 73 rd and has an overall grade of 43.7, ranking him 74 th out of 74 tackles. Bailey needs a bounce back game after last week’s disappointment. This is about as good as a get-right matchup that he’s going to get. This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: Jets vs. Dolphins: 3 key matchups to watch in Week 7

item.title: Weekend Warm-up: Bayern Munich has already showed heart, now its resilience will be tested
item.description: (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich proved something important against Arsenal — this team has heart, fight, and enough quality to go toe-to-toe with one of Europe’s strongest sides. The 2-2 draw in the Champions League was not the perfect result, but it was a reminder that Vincent Kompany’s squad is no t going to roll over just because a match gets uncomfortable. Now comes the next question: Can Bayern Munich put that performance behind them, get th eir legs moving again, and take care of business against SC Freiburg? If there is one thing Bundesliga football teaches you, it is t hat nobody cares how well you played three days ago when you show up on Sunday looking like you have spent the entire weekend celebrating a draw. Freiburg will not be interested in Bayern’s Champions League performance, the emotional satisfaction of competing with Ar senal, or how many encouraging things the Rekordmeister can take away from the match. They will be interested in making FC Bayern miserable, exploiting any signs of fatigue, and leaving the home side wondering why a perfectly manageable Bundesliga fixture suddenly feels like an escape room. And that is precise ly why this game matters. Freiburg is not here to be a “feel-good” story SC Freiburg migh t not have Arsenal’s star power, budget, or collection of expensive attacking toys, but dismissing Christian Streich’s former clu b would be a mistake. Under Julian Schuster, SC Freiburg has continued to be a well-organized, competitive side that understa nds how to make life difficult for opponents. The Black Forest club is disciplined, dangerous when they find opportunities to attack, and perfectly capable of punishing a team that gets sloppy. The Breisgau-Brasilianer are not going to roll out a red carpet and ask Harry Kane to help himself to a hat trick. They are going to compete, make the Bavarians work for space, and look for opportunities to turn small mistakes into big problems. That is what makes this a legitimate threat. Bayern should have the superior indivi dual quality. There is no reason to pretend otherwise. But superior quality does not automatically translate into three points, especially when t he schedule is crowded, recovery time is limited, and a team has just played an emotionally demanding European fixture. Bayern Munich has already shown that the y can respond to adversity within a match. The next step is showing they can respond to adversity across several games. item.content:encoded: (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich proved something important against Arsenal — this team has heart, fight, and enough quality to go toe-to-toe with one of Europe’s strongest sides. The 2-2 draw in the Champions League was not the perfect result, but it was a reminder that Vincent Kompany’s squad is no t going to roll over just because a match gets uncomfortable. Now comes the next question: Can Bayern Munich put that performance behind them, get th eir legs moving again, and take care of business against SC Freiburg? If there is one thing Bundesliga football teaches you, it is t hat nobody cares how well you played three days ago when you show up on Sunday looking like you have spent the entire weekend celebrating a draw. Freiburg will not be interested in Bayern’s Champions League performance, the emotional satisfaction of competing with Ar senal, or how many encouraging things the Rekordmeister can take away from the match. They will be interested in making FC Bayern miserable, exploiting any signs of fatigue, and leaving the home side wondering why a perfectly manageable Bundesliga fixture suddenly feels like an escape room. And that is precise ly why this game matters. Freiburg is not here to be a “feel-good” story SC Freiburg migh t not have Arsenal’s star power, budget, or collection of expensive attacking toys, but dismissing Christian Streich’s former clu b would be a mistake. Under Julian Schuster, SC Freiburg has continued to be a well-organized, competitive side that understa nds how to make life difficult for opponents. The Black Forest club is disciplined, dangerous when they find opportunities to attack, and perfectly capable of punishing a team that gets sloppy. The Breisgau-Brasilianer are not going to roll out a red carpet and ask Harry Kane to help himself to a hat trick. They are going to compete, make the Bavarians work for space, and look for opportunities to turn small mistakes into big problems. That is what makes this a legitimate threat. Bayern should have the superior indivi dual quality. There is no reason to pretend otherwise. But superior quality does not automatically translate into three points, especially when t he schedule is crowded, recovery time is limited, and a team has just played an emotionally demanding European fixture. Bayern Munich has already shown that the y can respond to adversity within a match. The next step is showing they can respond to adversity across several games. Can the Bavarians maintain th eir intensity without running themselves into the ground? Can they remain patient if Freiburg frustr ates them? Can they avoid the defensive lapses that turn a routine afternoon into a full-blown emergency? The answers will tell us plenty about the team’s maturity. Harry Kane cannot take his foot off the gas If Bayer n Munich is going to turn its Arsenal performance into momentum rather than a nice memory, Harry Kane will once again need to lead from the front. Kane has become much more than the guy waiting in the penalty area for someone to deliver a cross. He links play, drops into midfield, brings teammates into the a ttack, creates opportunities, and finishes them with the ruthless efficiency that makes defenders question their career choices. Kane’s performance against Arsenal demonstrated the importance of having a striker who can influence a match in multiple ways. Bayern Munich needs that same intelligence and quality again st SC Freiburg. Kane does not necessarily need to score three goals to have an excellent game. He needs to ke ep the attack connected, make smart decisions, occupy defenders, and create the space that allows Bayern Munich’s other attackers to do d amage. Of course, scoring a couple of goals would be nice. Nobody is asking him to become a selfless midfield conductor fo r 90 minutes when he is one of the best finishers in the world. The point is that Kane sets the tone. When he presses, competes, and demands the ball, the rest of the team has a standard to follow. Bayern Munich cannot afford to treat SC Freiburg as a lesser challenge simply because the opposition lacks Arsenal’s European pedigree. Michael Olise needs to keep being Michael Olise…on the field Then there is Michael Olise, who has become one of Bayern Munich’s m ost important attacking weapons. Olise brings creativity, composure, and the ability to make something happen when a defense appears to have everyt hing under control. His left foot can unlock compact defensive structures, and his decision-making gives Bayern another player capable of controlling the tempo in the final third. Against SC Freiburg, that could be especially important. If the home side sits deep, Bayern Munich will need players who can beat defenders, deliver dangerous passes, and find openings without forcing every attack through the middl e. Olise can provide all three. He can create chances for Kane, combine with the midfield, or take responsibility himself when the game needs a spark. But leadership is not just about producing one spectacular moment. It is about doing the difficult thi ngs consistently, even when the opponent is not glamorous and the match does not have a Champions League anthem playing in the background. Olise needs to bring the same concentration and ambition to Freiburg that he would bring to any European heavyweight. The Bundesliga title race does no t award bonus points for beating big teams if you then drop points against opponents you were expected to defeat. That is a lesson Bayern Munich has learned b efore. It does not need a refresher course. The real test is the response The Arsenal draw gave Bayern Munich something to build on. It showed resilience, attacking quality, and a willingness to keep fighting when the match became difficult. Those are meaningful pos itives, and Kompany deserves credit for the mentality his team displayed. But the schedule does not stop to let Bayern Munich admire themselv es in the mirror. SC Freiburg presents a different challenge, one that demands focus, discipline, and the ability to manage the emotional and physical hangover from European competition. Bayern Munich needs to start with energy, control the midfield, defend transitions properly, and avoid giving SC Freiburg reasons to believe they can take something from the match. Most importantly, the team must understand that bouncing back q uickly is about following a demanding performance with another professional one. That means no sluggish opening, no careless giveaways, and no treating SC Freiburg like an inconvenient appointment between Champions League nights. Bayern Munich showed its heart against Arsenal. Now it needs to show its consistency agai nst SC Freiburg. Kane and Olise must continue leading the attack, the supporting cast must match their intensity, and t he entire team needs to prove that its competitive fire burns just as brightly on a Sunday afternoon in the Bundesliga as it does under the Champions League lights. Because SC Freiburg is good enough to punish complacency, and Bayern Munich should be good enough to beat them — eve n when injured and tired. Now the boys need to prove it. Song of the Week: “Cherub Rock” by Smashing Pumpkins Diving back into the 90s, this one got a ton of airpla y, but seems to have drifted out of the radio consciousness (at least where I am). In the midst of a lot of different bands emerging, Smashing Pumpkins broke through in 1993 with the Siamese Dream albu m, and “Cherub Rock” was arguably the biggest hit. The song was everywhere, and all of a sudden, Sm ashing Pumpkins became a massive thing. These days, though, I do not know how many people truly remember how big they were at the time. item.title: Pittsburgh unveils honorary street sign for former world champion boxer
item.description: Pittsburgh city leaders unveiled a new street sign honoring a former world champion boxer 100 years after his death. The honorary “Harry Greb Way” is at the corner of Fifth Avenue and Washington Place, near where he previously trained — the Pittsburgh Lyceum. Officials also proclaimed Thursday “Harry Greb Day.” The recognition honors Greb’s roots in the city and seeks to preserve his memory as a local sports icon. Nicknamed “The Pittsburgh Windmill,” Greb held the world middleweight championship title from 1923 to 1926 before his death at age 32 after complications from surgery. Michael McSorley of the Conn-Greb Boxing Club spoke about the significance of this recognition. “For too long his name has been better known among boxing historians and around the world than amongst people here in his own hometown,” McSorley said. “Today helps change that.” During his boxing career, Greb achieved major historical milestones. In 1922, he became the first and only fighter to defeat boxing legend Gene Tunney. Over the course of his boxing career, Greb defeated 16 future Hall of Famers. item.title: Toprak Razgatlioglu Bids Farewell to the 2026 MotoGP Season Due to Injury
item.description: Pramac Yamaha Toprak Razgatlioglu Toprak Razgatlioglu is out for the remainder of the 2026 MotoGP season due to a right shoulder injury. This time last year, the racing world was alight with talk of how Toprak Razgatlioglu would do in his first MotoGP season at Pramac Yamaha. Now, with five rounds to go in the 2026 MotoGP season, he's in 21st position, and the only full-time MotoGP rider is Maverick Viñales, who missed a lot of this season due to injury. Unfortunately for Razgatlioglu, he is likely to fall even further down the rankings now that Viñales is back from injury and can score points, as 'El Turco' is out for the remainder of the 2026 MotoGP season. The three-time WorldSBK champion dislocated his right shoulder during a big crash in the second free practice of the Indonesian Grand Prix two weeks ago. Although the 30-year-old completed the sprint race, he retired during Sunday's race after just eight laps due to a lack of strength. After medical examinations in Milan, it was confirmed that the Turkish rider will undergo surgery on October 26th instead of waiting until the end of the season. This isn't surprising, given the fact that he could finish the remaining five rounds and not even end up in the top 20, all whilst putting his shoulder at far greater risk of more serious injury. All Things MotoGP Watching These Two MotoGP Racers Go-Karting Makes Me Realize How Much I'm Going To Miss Them Sega's Shadow the Hedgehog Motorcycle Sells for Insane Money for Ex-MotoGP Rider’s Charity Given the fact that this would've been Razgatlioglu's only chance to race at Philip Island on a MotoGP bike, he was extremely disappointed, saying, "I am extremely disappointed to miss the Australian Grand Prix. Phillip Island is one of my favorite circuits and a place where I experienced some very special moments during my Superbike career. I was really looking forward to the opportunity to compete there on a MotoGP bike, which makes this situation even harder to accept... Further medical examinations following the crash in Mandalika revealed that my shoulder injury is more serious than we initially thought. Therefore, I will undergo surgery in the coming days to give myself the best chance of a full recovery and a 100 percent return. This was not an easy decision, but after consulting with the doctors and those closest to me, we are convinced that this is the right step for my future." Yamaha test rider Augusto Fernandez will replace Razgatlioglu in the final five rounds of the season, and 'El Turco' will finish his rookie season with a score of 18 points.

item.title: Rockets-Spurs: Thompson Block & Sengun Buckets Put Houston Back In Business
item.description: Oct 23, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks the final shot attempt by San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) at the end of the game at Moody Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Houston Rockets sent a message with their Friday night 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs. The Rockets had already won their season opener on Wednesday. But in a sign of how far expectations had fallen for Houston this season, that matchup was against the lowly Dallas Mavericks. Just two games in, expectations are already on the rise. Rockets-Spurs Was the Rockets’ First Real Test Oct 23, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets center Alperen Sengun (28) and teammates react after Sengun scored while drawing a foul during the second half against the San Antonio Spurs at Moody Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs were a team that looked like they had Houston’s number last season. They had a lot of teams’ number, hence winding up as the second-last team standing, making it all the way to the NBA Finals. In particular, though, the Rockets looked like they had an Amen Thompson problem in Thompson’s matchup with Wembanyama . That matchup looked less problematic for the Rockets on Friday night, as the signature moment of it was Thompson swatting Wembanyama’s last-second shot attempt to tie. The block, which was on a post-up with Thompson as Wembanyama’s primary defender, sealed the game for Houston. Thompson also scored 20 points on 9-of-15 shooting, pulled in 10 rebounds, and added four assists and two steals to go with his two blocks. He even made 1-of-2 three-pointers. Caveats to Thompson’s Great Night There are some caveats to Thompson’s revenge game versus the Spurs, though. For one thing, Thompson was the only Rockets starter with a negative plus/minus. In 36 minutes of playtime, the Rockets were outscored by 12 points. That’s despite the Spurs declining to deploy their “secret” weapon against him. Wembanyama spent most of the game defending Alperen Şengün , rather than Thompson. Finally, Wembanyama is off to a bumpy start to 2026-27 in general. The seven-foot-“four” Frenchman went 9-of-21 from the field against the Rockets, which was a major improvement on the 1-of-13 he managed in the Spurs’ opener. Wembanyama’s impact is never limited to just his scoring. He has eight blocks already, two games into the season. But he didn’t seem quite prepared for just how hard opponents were going to lock in on shutting down his offense in 2026-27. The Spurs offense isn’t quite in Finals form just yet. Fred VanVleet ‘s return has made the Rockets’ offense look actually functional. item.content:encoded: Oct 23, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks the final shot attempt by San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) at the end of the game at Moody Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Houston Rockets sent a message with their Friday night 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs. The Rockets had already won their season opener on Wednesday. But in a sign of how far expectations had fallen for Houston this season, that matchup was against the lowly Dallas Mavericks. Just two games in, expectations are already on the rise. Rockets-Spurs Was the Rockets’ First Real Test Oct 23, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets center Alperen Sengun (28) and teammates react after Sengun scored while drawing a foul during the second half against the San Antonio Spurs at Moody Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs were a team that looked like they had Houston’s number last season. They had a lot of teams’ number, hence winding up as the second-last team standing, making it all the way to the NBA Finals. In particular, though, the Rockets looked like they had an Amen Thompson problem in Thompson’s matchup with Wembanyama . That matchup looked less problematic for the Rockets on Friday night, as the signature moment of it was Thompson swatting Wembanyama’s last-second shot attempt to tie. The block, which was on a post-up with Thompson as Wembanyama’s primary defender, sealed the game for Houston. Thompson also scored 20 points on 9-of-15 shooting, pulled in 10 rebounds, and added four assists and two steals to go with his two blocks. He even made 1-of-2 three-pointers. Caveats to Thompson’s Great Night There are some caveats to Thompson’s revenge game versus the Spurs, though. For one thing, Thompson was the only Rockets starter with a negative plus/minus. In 36 minutes of playtime, the Rockets were outscored by 12 points. That’s despite the Spurs declining to deploy their “secret” weapon against him. Wembanyama spent most of the game defending Alperen Şengün , rather than Thompson. Finally, Wembanyama is off to a bumpy start to 2026-27 in general. The seven-foot-“four” Frenchman went 9-of-21 from the field against the Rockets, which was a major improvement on the 1-of-13 he managed in the Spurs’ opener. Wembanyama’s impact is never limited to just his scoring. He has eight blocks already, two games into the season. But he didn’t seem quite prepared for just how hard opponents were going to lock in on shutting down his offense in 2026-27. The Spurs offense isn’t quite in Finals form just yet. Why Houston’s Offense Looks Better None of that should be overly concerning to Rockets fans. Right now, the team is healthy and firing on all cylinders. Fred VanVleet ‘s return has made the Rockets’ offense look actually functional. His 14 points on 4-of-10 shooting to go with five assists against the Spurs undersells the impact he’s already having compared with his absence last season. Şengün led all scorers in the game with 29 points on 10-of-20 shooting from the floor against the best defender in the NBA. He even went 4-of-6 in the fourth quarter, bamboozling San Antonio’s defense. Not only are Şengün All-NBA predictions looking strong early, but, so far, the work of the Rockets’ new shooting coach appears to be paying dividends as well. Thompson and Şengün Are Shooting Threes Shooting coach Chris Engelland worked extensively with Thompson and Şengün on their shooting this offseason. Either of them becoming non-liabilities from deep would be a legitimately era-defining development for the Rockets. Well, in the win versus the Spurs, Şengün shot 2-of-4 from three, including scoring the first three points of the game. He shot 2-of-2 against the Mavericks as well. Şengün started strong from three in 2025-26 before petering out. One encouraging difference this time around is that Thompson is also already 2-for-4 from three on the season. The low volume makes the numbers themselves mean very little, but it’s likely a point of emphasis for neither player to force three-pointers. The shot is never going to be what their game is built around, but if they have the confidence to shoot them when wide open, defenses will have to reconsider their approach to Houston’s offense. Add to the good news that Jabari Smith Jr. dropped a near-career-high 30 points in the Rockets opener, VanVleet grabbing at his leg during Friday night’s game turned out to be nothing, and Kevin Durant at 38 predictably still looks like Kevin Durant at 37. The Last Word The Rockets will play again on Saturday night versus the Atlanta Hawks in their first back-to-back of the season. Hopefully the team will take the cautious approach and rest returning players like VanVleet and Steven Adams . If Reed Sheppard can return from his previously day-to-day listed knee injury, even better. Busy in the midst of a back-to-back, the Rockets are back in business as a possible contender for the NBA title. item.title: Wake Up! Week 8 Viewing Guide and Morning Open Thread
item.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 17: The Million Dollar Band of Alabama before a game between the Tennessee Volunteers and Alabama Crimson Tide at Neyland Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Alabama is rolling into a homecoming game vs. a floundering Texas A&M squad after the Tide took back to back losses against Georgia and Tennessee. The good news is that pretty much everyone in the top ten lost last week, too. The bad news is that Alabama look utterly hapless doing it. In any case, this week begins the rest of a season where the Tide cannot afford a single slip up and still hope to have any shot. While we wait for that game in the 2:30 time slot, there’s also a decent slate of games this morning to keep you occupied and (hopefully) not fretting too much. Kicking things off in the SEC is #18 LSU vs Auburn. The WarPlainsmen are coming off an emotional high after upsetting Georgia, so there’s always the question of whether that’s a momentum that carries forward, or if they wind up falling utterly flat after such a crazy win the week before. Meanwhile, LSU is still looking to prove they can be one of the elite teams in the country. In the Big 10, you also have #6 Indiana taking on the 4-2 Michigan Wolverines. Michigan’s had a weird season, taking some weird losses but also some nice wins. Meanwhile, Indiana is reeling after losing their first game in 2 years. The ACC is trotting out #1 Miami vs Pitt. The Panthers have lost two straight games after a 5-0 start, and Miami is still rocking along as the odds on favorite to win the Natty this year. An upset seems unlikely…. But hey, never hurts to keep an eye on them with how college football has been going this season. Another interesting one could be the #8 Texas Tech vs Cincinnati game on FS1. The Red Raiders are quietly undefeated again, but they feel like a team that could slip up any week now. So enjoy the morning slate, and we’ll see you at 2:30. As always, the schedule below is in Central Time, and is courtesy of CFBGrid.com.

item.title: Paula Moltzan earns long-awaited first Alpine skiing World Cup win to open season
item.description: American Paula Moltzan earned her first Alpine skiing World Cup win after more than a decade since she started racing on the sport's highest level. Moltzan, 32, won the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden, Austria, rallying from fifth place after the opening run to win by one hundredth of a second over Albanian Lara Colturi combining times from two runs. "It feels like a fairytale right now, pretty unreal," Moltzan said. Moltzan, who debuted on the World Cup in 2012 and was dropped from the U.S. Ski Team ten years ago , had 10 second- or third-place finishes on the World Cup before Saturday. ALPINE SKIING: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule After winning her first Olympic medal last February (bronze in the team combined), Moltzan changed skis, becoming the lone woman on the World Cup to sign with Van Deer, the outfit founded by eight-time World Cup overall champion Marcel Hirscher. It paid off. She's the oldest woman to win her first World Cup. Mikaela Shiffrin had the fastest opening run by 14 hundredths of a second over Swede Sara Hector, then was 27th-fastest in the second run to drop to seventh overall. The men race a giant slalom in Soelden on Sunday at 5 a.m. and 8 a.m. ET, live on Peacock , which streams every race this season. Mikaela Shiffrin shifts World Cup race schedule for season of ‘exploration’ Mikaela Shiffrin is chasing curiosity in her 16th season on the World Cup. Nick Zaccardi ,

item.title: Indiana Fever’s reputation around the WNBA could stand in the way of a championship
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) talks with head coach Stephanie White during the first half of a WNBA game against the Chicago Sky at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images The Indiana Fever’s 2026 season ended abruptly after they were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs by the reigning champions, the Las Vegas Aces. And as the dust settles, criticism of the Fever’s future has continued to grow. During her exit interview, star guard Kelsey Mitchell reflected on the season and the battles she faced off the court over her association with Indiana and teammate Caitlin Clark, which she indicated could affect her decision as an unrestricted free agent this offseason. “Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard,” Mitchell said, via The Athletic . “I think this organization is unbelievable, man, but I think that when it comes to, like, really trying to be yourself, it hasn’t always been easy.” The backcourt duo of Mitchell and Clark was prolific this year, with both guards in MVP conversations. Losing Mitchell would obviously be a huge blow, but she may not be the Fever’s only concern. Annie Costabile and Brian Hamilton of The Athletic spoke with players, league executives, and dozens of agents about how the league perceives the Fever, who they described as “the molten-hot core of women’s professional basketball.” And many believe the franchise’s path is clouded. Hostile Environments According to several agents, many players around the WNBA dread playing against the Indiana Fever. “One agent said clients regularly disable social media accounts before and immediately after games against the Fever because of the increase in toxic messages they say they receive. Not all accounts clearly identify themselves as Fever fans. Harassment of Black players, in particular, has included racist messages following games against the Fever,” Costabile and Hamilton wrote. Another agent reportedly told The Athletic that clients have complained about being called the [N-word] at Fever games “multiple times.” “Online is always going to be worse,” this agent said, “but I’ve never had clients tell me they’ve been called certain names at any other arena other than Indy.” The Fever told The Athletic that they had not received any complaints about racial slurs from spectators at home games. More notably, Aces star A’ja Wilson was involved in an incident with a Fever fan during Game 2 of the first-round series and received a technical foul. Outraged, Wilson had a lot to say in her postgame press conference. “I try to play my game, keep it pushing. But if I’m just walking, because I had just got the foul, I’m chillin’, and I see a man come at me, taking steps towards me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said; I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone. That is unacceptable. You don’t step towards me,” Wilson said . Sophie Cunningham Sophie Cunningham
item.content:encoded: Aug 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) talks with head coach Stephanie White during the first half of a WNBA game against the Chicago Sky at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images The Indiana Fever’s 2026 season ended abruptly after they were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs by the reigning champions, the Las Vegas Aces. And as the dust settles, criticism of the Fever’s future has continued to grow. During her exit interview, star guard Kelsey Mitchell reflected on the season and the battles she faced off the court over her association with Indiana and teammate Caitlin Clark, which she indicated could affect her decision as an unrestricted free agent this offseason. “Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard,” Mitchell said, via The Athletic . “I think this organization is unbelievable, man, but I think that when it comes to, like, really trying to be yourself, it hasn’t always been easy.” The backcourt duo of Mitchell and Clark was prolific this year, with both guards in MVP conversations. Losing Mitchell would obviously be a huge blow, but she may not be the Fever’s only concern. Annie Costabile and Brian Hamilton of The Athletic spoke with players, league executives, and dozens of agents about how the league perceives the Fever, who they described as “the molten-hot core of women’s professional basketball.” And many believe the franchise’s path is clouded. Hostile Environments According to several agents, many players around the WNBA dread playing against the Indiana Fever. “One agent said clients regularly disable social media accounts before and immediately after games against the Fever because of the increase in toxic messages they say they receive. Not all accounts clearly identify themselves as Fever fans. Harassment of Black players, in particular, has included racist messages following games against the Fever,” Costabile and Hamilton wrote. Another agent reportedly told The Athletic that clients have complained about being called the [N-word] at Fever games “multiple times.” “Online is always going to be worse,” this agent said, “but I’ve never had clients tell me they’ve been called certain names at any other arena other than Indy.” The Fever told The Athletic that they had not received any complaints about racial slurs from spectators at home games. More notably, Aces star A’ja Wilson was involved in an incident with a Fever fan during Game 2 of the first-round series and received a technical foul. Outraged, Wilson had a lot to say in her postgame press conference. “I try to play my game, keep it pushing. But if I’m just walking, because I had just got the foul, I’m chillin’, and I see a man come at me, taking steps towards me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said; I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone. That is unacceptable. You don’t step towards me,” Wilson said . Sophie Cunningham Sophie Cunningham was at the center of negative media attention this season for the Fever, as her comments regarding transgender athletes in women’s sports sparked a season-long media frenzy. “I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,'” Cunningham said, via ESPN . “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.” Cunningham later doubled down on her comments , making matters worse for her and the team. “I said what I said. I think it’s kind of common sense, and I think I’ll always believe in that. I think it’s really important to protect children, and that’s little girls who are also involved in that category. I stand on what I said.” Cunningham is now a free agent, and one agent told The Athletic that they don’t believe she is worth the risk. But the same agent believes some team will sign her anyway, purely for her media draw. “Because of the money. People come watch her. Not because she’s the greatest basketball player. Because of what she does.” The Caitlin Clark Effect Clark has been one of the biggest influences in women’s basketball and also one of the most talented. But because of her large notoriety, players and even teammates can get lost in her orbit. “There is such a microscope on me,” Clark said during her postseason news conference. “And that kind of comes with everybody else I’ve been teammates with, whether that was my time at Iowa, whether that’s been here. It comes with a lot of really great things. And then at times there can be some negatives.” Though she acknowledged her stardom, many agents believe the Fever have been slow to address these issues because the team doesn’t want to alienate fans or risk losing revenue. The Fever have the entire offseason to address any locker room issues they’ve incurred, but the question of star guard Kelsey Mitchell’s return may be the least of their worries if they’re aiming at title contention next year. The post Indiana Fever’s reputation around the WNBA could stand in the way of a championship appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Jose Mourinho laughs off ‘superstition’ claims over new beard as Real Madrid take perfect October into El Clasico
item.description: Real Madrid v Sevilla FC - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jose Mourinho has laughed off suggestions that his recently grown beard is the secret behind Real Madrid's flawless run of form. The Portuguese tactician faces a massive test this weekend as his side prepares to travel to the Camp Nou for a high-stakes El Clasico. The transformation of Los Blancos The landscape at the Santiago Bernabeu looked considerably bleaker just over a month ago. On September 20, Madrid suffered a painful 2-1 defeat in the capital derby against Atletico, a result that left them languishing in fourth place and trailing arch-rivals Barcelona by six points. It was a period of intense scrutiny for Mourinho, whose visible frustration mirrored the team's struggling domestic form following an earlier slip-up against Real Betis. However, the narrative has shifted dramatically in the weeks since that derby disappointment. Madrid have embarked on an exceptional winning streak that has spanned both La Liga and the Champions League. This tactical and mental turnaround has coincided with a change in Mourinho’s physical appearance, as the manager has opted to grow out a beard during this successful period, leading to light-hearted chatter regarding his new routine. Mourinho denies superstitious motives During a recent press conference, the manager was directly questioned about whether his facial hair had become a lucky charm during this run of four consecutive victories. "Has he had a beard for a month and won everything: is it superstition?" he was asked. The inquiry prompted an immediate and amused reaction from the former Chelsea and Inter boss. Mourinho was quick to dismiss the idea that his grooming habits were linked to the team's fortunes on the pitch. "Absolutely not," he replied with a smile, as reported by Sky Sport Italia . "Do I look that bad? Should I shave it? But I am one of the few in the world of football not to be superstitious." Maintaining momentum in October Despite his denials, the statistical evidence of October is hard to ignore for those looking for patterns. Sky Sport Italia noted, the winning run began with a gritty 1-0 victory over Villarreal, secured by a goal from Yan Diomande. This was followed by a thrilling 4-3 comeback win against Roma in the Champions League, where late strikes from Endrick and Antonio Rudiger turned the game on its head in the final minutes of play. The clinical nature of Madrid's performances continued as they swept aside Sevilla with a 4-1 scoreline in La Liga. Kylian Mbappe was the protagonist in that fixture, netting twice to ensure the three points stayed in the capital. The momentum carried over into their next European assignment against RB Leipzig, which ended in another emphatic 4-1 triumph thanks to goals from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Mbappe, and Diomande. Kylian Mbappe was the protagonist in that fixture, netting twice to ensure the three points stayed in the capital. The momentum carried over into their next European assignment against RB Leipzig, which ended in another emphatic 4-1 triumph thanks to goals from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Mbappe, and Diomande. This sequence of results has restored confidence within the squad at a pivotal moment in the campaign. Mourinho’s side appears to have found a balance that was missing during the opening weeks of the season, setting the stage for the most significant test of their credentials yet. The ultimate test at Camp Nou The upcoming El Clasico at Camp Nou presents a unique challenge for the bearded Mourinho. Barcelona enter the contest with a perfect domestic record, having won seven out of seven matches in La Liga so far. However, the Catalan giants are coming off their first defeat of the season, a loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, which may provide a psychological opening for the visiting side. Madrid still find themselves trailing by six points in the league table, making this encounter vital if they wish to close the gap on the leaders. The match will also be played without Vinicius Junior, who is serving a four-match suspension.

item.title: Johann Zarco retires from Australian GP sprint: It was “dangerous” to continue
item.description: Motorsport photo Johann Zarco says he was forced to retire from the sprint race for the Australian Grand Prix after an electronic problem made it “dangerous” for him to continue riding. The LCR rider had been one of the star performers in qualifying at Phillip Island, taking advantage of wet conditions to progress through Q1 before putting his satellite Honda on the front row behind the Ducatis of Marc Marquez and Alex Marquez . However, his race lasted just three full laps before he was forced to peel into the pits with what technical gremlins, bringing a premature end to his day. Speaking afterwards, Zarci explained that a faulty gearbox sensor meant he could no longer see which gear he was in on the dashboard. He also pointed to a larger electronic issue that impacted the handling of the bike, ultimately making it impossible for him to continue. “Unlucky,” he said, describing his early exit from the sprint. “I got a technical problem. I got a sensor on the gearbox that I think got broken because the bike was lost; I didn't know in which gear I was. Johann Zarco, Team LCR Honda, Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team “I got some strange behaviour of the bike in some corners. Then I saw that I could not ride anymore and it was even becoming dangerous because with this powerful bike and with the electronics, and the gearbox doesn't know where it is…. “It's not a mechanical problem; it was an electronic problem. I could not fight. “Already the bike was giving a strange feeling in TC and also in engine brake, and when I understood what was happening, I stopped; it was just too dangerous.” Zarco held third position on the opening lap of the sprint, losing one spot to a fast-starting Jorge Martin but passing the Gresini Ducati of Alex Marquez. He dropped behind Marquez and Pedro Acosta on the next tour, but was still running comfortably inside the top five when he was forced to slow down on lap 4. With Zarco retiring early, Joan Mir absent all weekend due to illness and Luca Marini withdrawing on Saturday morning due to a virus, Diogo Moreira was left as the only Honda rider in the sprint. The LCR rookie took the chequered flag in ninth place, but was promoted to eighth after Trackhouse’s Ai Ogura was hit with an eight-second time penalty for a tyre pressure infringement. While the sprint took place in dry conditions, heavy rain is forecast at Phillip Island during the grand prix on Sunday, when Zarco and Moreira will be the only representatives from Honda on a depleted 18-bike MotoGP grid. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Johann Zarco says he was forced to retire from the sprint race for the Australian Grand Prix after an electronic problem made it “dangerous” for him to continue riding. The LCR rider had been one of the star performers in qualifying at Phillip Island, taking advantage of wet conditions to progress through Q1 before putting his satellite Honda on the front row behind the Ducatis of Marc Marquez and Alex Marquez . However, his race lasted just three full laps before he was forced to peel into the pits with what technical gremlins, bringing a premature end to his day. Speaking afterwards, Zarci explained that a faulty gearbox sensor meant he could no longer see which gear he was in on the dashboard. He also pointed to a larger electronic issue that impacted the handling of the bike, ultimately making it impossible for him to continue. “Unlucky,” he said, describing his early exit from the sprint. “I got a technical problem. I got a sensor on the gearbox that I think got broken because the bike was lost; I didn't know in which gear I was. Johann Zarco, Team LCR Honda, Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team “I got some strange behaviour of the bike in some corners. Then I saw that I could not ride anymore and it was even becoming dangerous because with this powerful bike and with the electronics, and the gearbox doesn't know where it is…. “It's not a mechanical problem; it was an electronic problem. I could not fight. “Already the bike was giving a strange feeling in TC and also in engine brake, and when I understood what was happening, I stopped; it was just too dangerous.” Zarco held third position on the opening lap of the sprint, losing one spot to a fast-starting Jorge Martin but passing the Gresini Ducati of Alex Marquez. He dropped behind Marquez and Pedro Acosta on the next tour, but was still running comfortably inside the top five when he was forced to slow down on lap 4. With Zarco retiring early, Joan Mir absent all weekend due to illness and Luca Marini withdrawing on Saturday morning due to a virus, Diogo Moreira was left as the only Honda rider in the sprint. The LCR rookie took the chequered flag in ninth place, but was promoted to eighth after Trackhouse’s Ai Ogura was hit with an eight-second time penalty for a tyre pressure infringement. While the sprint took place in dry conditions, heavy rain is forecast at Phillip Island during the grand prix on Sunday, when Zarco and Moreira will be the only representatives from Honda on a depleted 18-bike MotoGP grid. item.title: Roberto Martinez hails Nico Paz: ‘It’s like watching Maradona’
item.description: Roberto Martinez hails Nico Paz: ‘It’s like watching Maradona’ Roberto Martinez has compared Nico Paz to Diego Maradona after the Argentine inspired Como to a stunning 4-1 Champions League win over Manchester United. The 22-year-old was named Player of the Match on Wednesday, scoring twice and setting up another as Cesc Fabregas’ side swept aside the Premier League giants at the Sinigaglia. Working as a UEFA Technical Observer, Martinez was full of praise in an analysis on UEFA’s official website . “He executed two goals and an assist in the first three goals. That’s star material,” the former Belgium coach said. “It was like watching Maradona, watching that type of player that gets the team on his shoulders.” ARLINGTON, TEXAS – JULY 06: Roberto Martinez, Head Coach of Portugal, looks on before the FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 match between Portugal and Spain at Dallas Stadium on July 06, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Martinez on Nico Paz: ‘The execution was perfect’ Nico Paz opened the scoring inside two minutes and then set up Tasos Douvikas early in the second half, his third assist of the league phase. His second goal came from Fabregas’ high press, as he robbed Carlos Baleba and ran 25 metres before finishing. “I love Nico’s clinical touch. He’s a wonderful footballer with great balance and likes to have the ball in close control,” said Martínez, who led Portugal to Nations League glory in 2025. “You could see the space that he had. The execution was perfect.” OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) It caps a superb few weeks for Paz, who recently scored in three successive friendlies for Argentina. “It’s one of the most special nights in my life, in my career,” the Como star said. “Not only for me but also for the club and the fans.” Paz was left out of the Como starting XI for Saturday’s home game against Sassuolo.

item.title: Beppe Bergomi finds fault in Luciano Spalletti’s decisions
item.description: Beppe Bergomi finds fault in Luciano Spalletti’s decisions Inter Milan legend Beppe Bergomi has shared his thoughts on Juventus’ difficult season, identifying the club’s frequent changes of formation as one of the factors contributing to their struggles in Turin. Luciano Spalletti was expected to have settled on a preferred tactical approach after spending time experimenting with different systems last season. The manager made several adjustments in search of the right balance for his squad, hoping to establish a structure that would bring greater consistency to the team. However, Juventus have continued to switch formations since the beginning of the current campaign. Their efforts to find a reliable system have also been complicated by a persistent injury crisis, leaving Spalletti with limited options when selecting his starting eleven. Juventus continue to struggle with consistency The Bianconeri have suffered numerous injuries this season , with fresh cases emerging every few weeks. Several players have remained unavailable for extended periods, preventing the club from restoring its squad to full strength and allowing the manager to work with his preferred group of players. As a result, Juventus have been left with fewer options across the pitch, making it difficult to maintain the same formation and tactical approach from one match to the next. The situation has added to their difficulties as they attempt to find consistency and improve their performances. Frequent changes may be understandable when injuries force a manager to adapt, but they can also make it harder for players to develop familiarity with their roles. Spalletti must therefore balance the need to respond to absences with the importance of establishing a recognisable style of play. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Bergomi questions Juventus’ tactical changes Bergomi has now weighed in on the situation, suggesting that Juventus’ repeated adjustments to their playing system are not helping the team at present. Speaking via Calciomercato , the Inter Milan icon assessed their performance and highlighted the tactical approach used during the match. ” They didn’t have a good game. They struggled in the first half , but they broke the deadlock right away, but after that I think that constantly changing playing systems doesn’t help you have time. “Today we had a 3-5-2 with McKennie’s position being a bit unusual as he switched between them, but it’s basically a 3-5-2.” His comments underline the challenge facing Spalletti as he tries to bring stability to Juventus. While injuries continue to limit his choices, establishing a consistent formation could help the available players develop better understanding and improve the team’s overall performances. For now, Juventus must find a way to manage their absences while building greater tactical continuity.

item.title: Official statement – Deliberative Council
item.description: Official statement – Deliberative Council On September 28, the Deliberative Council held its final meeting on the revision of the Bylaws proposed by the Bylaws Committee. This followed months of debate and voting on all amendments proposed by Council members, each of which was considered individually. Once all amendments had been voted on, all articles that had not been amended were voted on as a block. The new Bylaws were approved by an overwhelming majority of the Deliberative Council, with the Council’s presiding officers tasked with emailing Council members the consolidated text of what had been approved so that they could identify any inconsistencies. That text was duly sent on October 21 for review, and access to audio recordings of all meetings was also made available to clear up any questions. Only one Council member requested the link. At the end of the final meeting, Council members were congratulated on approving the Bylaws and on the work they had carried out over several months for the benefit of the club. The procedure for addressing any inconsistencies in the text was clearly explained, and none of them raised any objection. It is therefore surprising that, at this stage before notice is issued for the General Meeting of members, some should express surprise at something already approved by the full Deliberative Council, particularly when many of the approved amendments were their own proposals. It should also be noted that there will be a period of 19 (nineteen) days between the circulation of the consolidated text and the scheduled date of the General Meeting of members—more than enough time to identify any corrections needed in the text circulated. A few Council members are already doing so: rather than taking inaccurate information to news outlets and social media, they are doing what was agreed, namely reviewing the text and identifying any inconsistencies so that, once corrected, the text can be sent to Council members again and subsequently made available to club members. The presiding officers of the Deliberative Council have no interest whatsoever in changing the approved text, and the audio recordings and their transcripts leave no room for dispute. Regarding the irresponsible allegation that the presiding officers are violating provisions of the current Bylaws and the Deliberative Council’s Rules of Procedure, we offer the following clarifications. Article 163, paragraph 2, of the Rules of Procedure establishes that, following approval of an amendment to or revision of the Bylaws, notice of a General Meeting to review and decide on the proposal must be ISSUED within 30 (thirty) days.
