item.content:encoded: Official statement – Deliberative Council On September 28, the Deliberative Council held its final meeting on the revision of the Bylaws proposed by the Bylaws Committee. This followed months of debate and voting on all amendments proposed by Council members, each of which was considered individually. Once all amendments had been voted on, all articles that had not been amended were voted on as a block. The new Bylaws were approved by an overwhelming majority of the Deliberative Council, with the Council’s presiding officers tasked with emailing Council members the consolidated text of what had been approved so that they could identify any inconsistencies. That text was duly sent on October 21 for review, and access to audio recordings of all meetings was also made available to clear up any questions. Only one Council member requested the link. At the end of the final meeting, Council members were congratulated on approving the Bylaws and on the work they had carried out over several months for the benefit of the club. The procedure for addressing any inconsistencies in the text was clearly explained, and none of them raised any objection. It is therefore surprising that, at this stage before notice is issued for the General Meeting of members, some should express surprise at something already approved by the full Deliberative Council, particularly when many of the approved amendments were their own proposals. It should also be noted that there will be a period of 19 (nineteen) days between the circulation of the consolidated text and the scheduled date of the General Meeting of members—more than enough time to identify any corrections needed in the text circulated. A few Council members are already doing so: rather than taking inaccurate information to news outlets and social media, they are doing what was agreed, namely reviewing the text and identifying any inconsistencies so that, once corrected, the text can be sent to Council members again and subsequently made available to club members. The presiding officers of the Deliberative Council have no interest whatsoever in changing the approved text, and the audio recordings and their transcripts leave no room for dispute. Regarding the irresponsible allegation that the presiding officers are violating provisions of the current Bylaws and the Deliberative Council’s Rules of Procedure, we offer the following clarifications. Article 163, paragraph 2, of the Rules of Procedure establishes that, following approval of an amendment to or revision of the Bylaws, notice of a General Meeting to review and decide on the proposal must be ISSUED within 30 (thirty) days. The final meeting took place on September 28, as noted above, which means that the Council President has until October 28 to ISSUE NOTICE of the General Meeting. Furthermore, the main provision of Article 26 of the current Bylaws states that “notice of General Meetings shall be issued by the President of the Deliberative Council: (a) 30 (thirty) days in advance for Ordinary General Meetings and for an Extraordinary General Meeting convened to decide on the matter provided for in subparagraph ‘a’, item II, of Article 25 of these Bylaws; and (b) 15 (fifteen) days in advance for all other Extraordinary General Meetings.” Item II of Article 25 concerns Extraordinary General Meetings, and subparagraph “a”, the only provision requiring 30 (thirty) days’ advance notice , concerns submitting the following matter to members: “filling vacancies in the offices of President and Vice-President of the Management Committee should they arise during the term of office, in the circumstances provided for in these Bylaws.” Amendments to the Bylaws are covered by subparagraph “b” , meaning that 15 (fifteen) days’ advance notice is required. Nor is it valid to argue, as has been reported, that the main provision of Article 6 of the Rules of Procedure requires 30 (thirty) days’ notice, since it cannot override what is established in the Bylaws. That would be like a decree containing a provision contrary to the law it implements. On that point, the decree would be deemed unlawful, as it is a lower-ranking legal instrument. Confident that the presiding officers of the Deliberative Council are acting in accordance with the current Bylaws and its Rules of Procedure, they reiterate that the sovereignty of the club’s members will prevail. item.title: Can Max Dowman fill Bukayo Saka’s spot at Arsenal?
item.description: Can Max Dowman fill Bukayo Saka’s spot at Arsenal? Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Max Dowman will get minutes in Bukayo Saka’s absence, but he needs time to build the habits of a more senior Premier League player. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images Bukayo Saka is reportedly set to miss the next couple of months of action with Arsenal , leaving the Gunners in a tricky situation with their attacking options. Noni Madueke is the usual alternative to Saka, but he’s been needed on the left in Christos Tzolis’ absence. Eberechi Eze can also play on the left, as he showed in midweek, but beyond Madueke and Eze there are very few available options. 16-year-old Max Dowman is one of them, and the teenager appears to have made the squad to face Everton on Saturday. Speaking ahead of the game, Mikel Arteta answered questions about whether Dowman would get chances in Saka’s absence. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images “He’s training, and every time he’s got a moment to play, he’s showing that he’s a player who is going to impact the game, so for sure he’s going to have minutes,” Arteta said (via Arsenal.com and HaytersTV ). “Here (at Arsenal) it’s different (to other clubs), and the margins are much smaller, and he needs to be able to do that, but understanding where he is as well, you know? “He’s someone that really wants to learn, and he really wants to do it. He just needs the habit, and a habit takes some time to do it. “What we cannot take is the talent, the freedom, and the capacity that he has to do the things that are not on that piece of paper and the ones that you haven’t described, because he is unique at doing that.” Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images At such a young age, Dowman has already made a first-team impact at Arsenal on multiple occasions. There was the penalty he won against Leeds United last season, the iconic goal against Everton , and the Player of the Round performance he put in against Ipswich Town last month. The question is really just whether he’s ready to do it on a consistent basis. Most players his age aren’t playing first-team football at all. Even the footballers who have played in the Premier League at 16 through the years generally only got a moment or two. It would be unprecedented in the division’s history for Dowman to get a run of starts. It wouldn’t be the first time Dowman had done something no one had done before, but it’s up to Arteta whether he thinks this latest challenge is one the teenager is capable of living up to. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images

item.title: Bills news: Previewing potential trade targets and positional needs
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Amik Robertson #2 of the Washington Commanders looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Buffalo Bills on their bye week, Brandon Beane, Joe Brady and the rest of the front office staff are using this time to review what has gone right, what has gone wrong, and how the team can improve if it wants to finally win the franchise’s first Super Bowl. The NFL’s trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 10, and with the offense scoring at a historic clip and the defense allowing almost every opponent to hang around, Beane and co. would be wise to explore every opportunity to bring in talent for the stretch run. Bills Mafia! Download the SB Nation app today! Bring the energy of game day wherever you go and share every reaction with fellow members of the Bills Mafia. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by examining Buffalo’s positions of need and exploring the best available players who have been linked to the Bills, including Miami Dolphins talented off-ball linebacker Jordyn Brooks (pictured below), who carries a minimal cap hit this year and is under contract for 2027 at $13M guaranteed. Check out the news items below and then let us know your thoughts on who Brandon Beane should acquire before the trade deadline in the comments section. Previewing Buffalo’s needs and potential fits at the trade deadline For as good as the offense has been through the first six weeks, the team could use another wide receiver with veteran DJ Moore missing four of the first six games and Joshua Palmer battling a case of the drops. But any offensive needs pale in comparison to the defensive side of the ball, where Buffalo could consider shoring up the safety, inside linebacker, and cornerback positions. Linked below: we run through the top options who are expected to be on the trading block at this year’s trade deadline; identify a few potential fits for the Bills, including Miami linebacker Jordyn Brooks, Washington Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson (pictured below), Titans safety Amani Hooker, Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker, Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, and Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson; and more! item.title: King Vogt and the Guardians of the Round Table (A cathartic chapter)
item.description: King Vogt and the Guardians of the Round Table — by Mario Crescibene I. The Battle of Lake Erie Introduction Chapter 1 Chapter 2 Chapter 3 II. The Quest for the Holy Grail Interlude Chapter 4 Chapter 5 Chapter 6 III. The King of the Wind Chapter 7 Chapter 8 Chapter 9 Chapter 10 Chapter 11 IV. The King of the Sea Chapter 12 Chapter 13 Chapter 14 Interlude Part II. I sat up briskly in my hammock, leaned over the edge, and threw up in the bucket next to me. “What was that?” I asked the Shaman as he stirred in his chair. item.content:encoded: King Vogt and the Guardians of the Round Table — by Mario Crescibene I. The Battle of Lake Erie Introduction Chapter 1 Chapter 2 Chapter 3 II. The Quest for the Holy Grail Interlude Chapter 4 Chapter 5 Chapter 6 III. The King of the Wind Chapter 7 Chapter 8 Chapter 9 Chapter 10 Chapter 11 IV. The King of the Sea Chapter 12 Chapter 13 Chapter 14 Interlude Part II. I sat up briskly in my hammock, leaned over the edge, and threw up in the bucket next to me. “What was that?” I asked the Shaman as he stirred in his chair. I slowly came back to the small cabin in the jungle, the nighttime sounds resonating all around me. “It was just a story, hermanito,” he said comfortingly. “I didn’t like it,” I said, rolling over in the hammock, trying to find a position that wouldn’t make me feel nauseous. “There was a giant eye that ruled over this space like an M.C. Escher painting… that part was cool. But the ending got really intense when King Vogt and the Guardians took on the King of the Sea. I thought the Guardians of the Round Table were destined to claim the Commissioner’s Trophy. But at the end of the story they were trapped inside this purple hurricane, on a tiny boat, facing a fleet of four sloops-of-war and a sea monster from the deep.” I rolled over again as a bubble rose in my chest and a sulfurous burp escaped. “Ugh. I believed it was their destiny to finally win… and then it was like they were destined to fail the whole time. Tampa made all the plays they needed to, and we didn’t. Losing stinks.” The Shaman used his shakapa to fan the lingering stench of the sulfurous burp. “It does, hermano. But it was all just a story. And every story has important lessons. Our destiny can seem manifest… until it isn’t. Do you know that we are living in the time of a great prophecy that is told throughout Indigenous cultures across the Americas?” “I didn’t,” I sighed, finally finding a better position. “Tell me about it.” “This is an era foretold by many ancient civilizations,” the Shaman began. “The natives throughout the Americas speak of The Prophecy of the Eagle and the Condor . It tells of a time when the Eagle People of the North — the cultures of science, the mind, and logic — have all the power; while the Condor People of the South — cultures of the arts, the heart, and faith — have very little. But the prophecy says that during this time, there will be an opportunity to reconnect the people of the Americas, and a sharing of wisdom that will unite them as one. That unification will result in a collective transformation that will bring about a new era in the history of mankind. But… the prophecy is clear that this is merely an opportunity…. it is not destined to happen. This is the moment, but we must take advantage of it.” The Shaman’s words reminded me of one of my favorite quotes. “There’s a line from Field of Dreams that says:” ‘There comes a time when all the cosmic tumblers have clicked into place and the universe opens itself up for a few seconds to show you what’s possible.’ “But I guess once those few seconds pass, the universe slams shut again, and what was once possible isn’t possible anymore. Sounds a lot like the Guardians this year,” I mumbled, sinking deeper into the support of the hammock. “A season of possibilities, and missed opportunities.” “So then let’s change the topic since losses stinks for a while,” the Shaman said as he got up. “And I’ll light some palo santo.” As the Shaman lit the ends of the wooden sticks, he continued, “So you like the knights, but not the part in the story when they are about to lose to the giant devil ray.” “Knights are the best,” I said excitedly, feeling some of my energy returning. “King Arthur was one of my favorite stories growing up. The biggest question each day was whether I was going to dress up as King Arthur or Percival.” “Then let’s continue with the knight theme, but we’ll shift our perspective,” the Shaman said as he took the burning ends of palo santo and waved the sweet smelling smoke around the small cabin. “I may live in the jungle, but we do have movie theaters here, and I really enjoyed Monty Python and the Holy Grail when they showed it. So since we need some humor and you like King Arthur, let’s focus on one of those famous scenes from the Holy Grail . Do you like the scene when the two peasants are debating with King Arthur?” “Oh, I do!” I said, already remembering the hilarious exchange between King Arthur and the muddy peasants. “And you hate Paul Dolan, which is why you made him Morgan le Fay reincarnate.” “He’s so cheap. Imagine what this team could have done if they had a few key players to support José. I can’t wait for Dolan to give up ownership.” “Well let’s focus on that then,” the Shaman said. “The day when the Dread Warlock Dolan leaves Cleveland. We can imagine him riding out on a horse as he passes the two peasants in the mud…” DOLAN: (beckons to one of the Peasants standing in the mud) You there! The one caked in mud. Which way leads out of Cleveland? PEASANT 1: (Turns toward Dolan and half-acknowledges him) This isn’t mud. DOLAN: What? PEASANT 1: I’m not caked in mud. DOLAN: Well, you’re standing in mud, and I can see that your shirt is clearly brown. PEASANT 1: It’s a Browns jersey. That’s why it’s brown. DOLAN: Forgive me, but from a distance it looked like you were caked in mud. You are, after all, in the mud. PEASANT 1: Oh, in the mud, yes. We’ve been in the mud ever since Deshaun Watson. But caked in mud? No. DOLAN: (getting frustrated) Semantics! (A second Browns fan, who was also standing in the mud — but most certainly not caked in it — comes over.) PEASANT 2: (taunting) Oh, semantics, says the big Dread Warlock. DOLAN: I’ll have you know I am a billionaire! PEASANT 2: Oh, a billionaire, ’e says. Very nice. And ’ow’d you get that, eh? By exploitin’ the people! Cryin’ poor, all the while hoardin’ away profits under yer down mattress. Or did Daddy Warbucks come back from the Crusades with a nice big stash of gold for ye? DOLAN: (getting more frustrated) Can you just tell me the way out of Cleveland?! PEASANT 1: The rich billionaire didn’t think to buy a map, did ’e? PEASANT 2: You know what else ’e didn’t think of? Tradin’ for Jo Adell before the season started. That coulda made a real difference, havin’ a full season of a right-handed power hitter. PEASANT 1: It could ’ave indeed, it could ’ave indeed. You know what else ’e didn’t think of… thinkin’ to sign Foster Griffin in the offseason instead of trading for ‘im at the deadline. And what did Griffin sign for? I ask you. What did ’e sign for? PEASANT 2: What did ’e sign for? PEASANT 1: $5.5 million, for the year. But no way a billionaire can afford ‘at! No sir. (wagging his finger) We must be frugal with the family funds! PEASANT 2: And havin’ an arm like Griffin’s for a full season would’ve saved the other pitchers too. Those pitchers were runnin’ on fumes by the end. But did ’e think of that? Did ’e? PEASANT 1: Indeed ’e did not! And you know what else ’e didn’t think of? DOLAN: (through gritted teeth) The way. Out. Of Cleveland. PEASANT 2: (ignoring Dolan completely) Do tell, my unjustly-accused-of-bein’-mud-caked friend. PEASANT 1: They didn’t think to take the Guardians to the Armor Court at the Cleveland Museum of Art. The Guardians liked Medieval Times so much that they bought a helmet and sword — but no one thought to take ’em to the world-renowned art museum where an entire armor court awaits ’em?! — with a sword equal to Excalibur itself that was wielded by a lord! They could ’ave taken their media team and documented the whole thing. Woulda been a great opportunity. Maybe the museum would ’ave let ’em touch a real battle-used sword. PEASANT 2: They should hire ye to do their marketin’ campaigns. PEASANT 1: Oh, the Dread Warlock Dolan could never afford me! ’E whines about low revenue, and cries poor over ticket sales, but then why doesn’t

item.title: Tilak Varma's versatility hailed: Ex-players, fans praise India's crisis man as MI star guides India to an epic run chase vs New Zealand
item.description: Tilak Varma's versatility hailed: Ex-players, fans praise India's crisis man as MI star guides India to an epic run chase vs New Zealand originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Tilak Varma made an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls to win the second T20I for India vs New Zealand . India were 70 for 5 and then 112 for 6 before Tilak and Nitish Kumar Reddy rescued the chase. Former India star Irfan Pathan praised Tilak's ability to bat anywhere in the order. Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 rescues India from 70 for 5 at Hagley Oval Tilak Varma has pulled India out of trouble for the last couple of years, but the version of it he produced in Christchurch on Saturday was something else. India were 70 for 5 chasing 181 in the 2nd T20I at Christchurch, and he finished unbeaten on 51 from 26 balls, taking them home with a ball to spare. Mitchell Santner had torn through the top order to leave the chase in ruins, the New Zealand captain eventually finishing with 4 for 21. When Naman Dhir fell for 31 in the 15th over, India were 112 for 6 and still needed 69 from 31 deliveries with only Nitish Kumar Reddy and the tail to come. What followed was an unbroken seventh-wicket stand of 69 off just 30 balls. Seventeen came off Jacob Duffy's third over, and Tilak then took four boundaries off Nathan Smith in the penultimate over to swing it decisively before Reddy, unbeaten on 26 from 13, hit the winning runs. Tilak batted at number six on the night, below a promoted Axar Patel, and his six fours and a six came at a strike rate of 196. New Zealand will reflect on a dropped chance at point from Bevon Jacobs that gave him a life and on a total of 180 for 5 built around Glenn Phillips' 70 and Jacobs' 58 that proved 11 runs short. MORE: 'Fielding like Pakistan': NZ fielders trolled after failing to defend 180 vs India Irfan Pathan says Tilak Varma's versatility puts him in a different league Among the former players who weighed in afterwards, Irfan Pathan focused less on the runs than on where they came from, pointing to a batter who has now delivered from almost every position in the order. "Versatility of Tilak Varma is Admirable. This win came on the back of his sheer ability to bat anywhere, and to be able to deliver under pressure puts him in a different league," Pathan said . Versatility of Tilak Varma is Admirable. This win came on the back of his sheer ability to bat anywhere and to be able to deliver under pressure puts him in a diffrent league. — Irfan Pathan (@IrfanPathan) October 24, 2026 Author Niket Soni admitted he had written the match off before the stand began and spread the credit between both unbeaten batters. "WHAT A GAME! At one point, I genuinely thought it was over. But what a comeback! Take a bow, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy! Cricket is never over until it's over!" Soni wrote . "Tilak Verma is one heck of a player. This guy is building a Dhoniish reputation when it comes to finishing. What a knock!!!" one fan wrote . Tilak Verma is one heck of a player. This guy is building a Dhoniish reputation when it comes to finishing. What a knock!!! — Mohammad Aizaz (@SeedaBalla93) October 24, 2026 Another laid out the situation he walked into alongside the numbers he produced, and the contrast between the two did most of the work. "TAKE A BOW, TILAK VERMA. Team India at one point 70/5, and he came in under pressure, and he smashed 51* runs from 26 balls, including 6 fours and 1 six in a successful run chase - What a Knock by Tilak," they posted . TAKE A BOW, TILAK VERMA.🙇 Team India at one point 70/5 and he came in under pressure and he smashed 51* runs from 26 balls including 6 fours and 1 six in successful run chase - What a Knock by Tilak. 👏 pic.twitter.com/b9NVunyisV — Tanuj (@ImTanujSingh) October 24, 2026 One supporter spread the credit further down the card, remembering the 31 from Naman Dhir that kept India within range before the final stand began. "What a match. What a knock from Tilak Varma, and Nitish Kumar Reddy's knock was special too. Also, special thanks to Naman Dhir. Well done, team India," they wrote . What a match what a knock from Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy's knock was special too also special thanks to Naman dhir well done team India. — Kevin (@imkevin149) October 24, 2026 Reddy, with his 26 off 13, and Dhir, with his 17-ball-31, also played a major role in India's win against the Kiwis. MORE: 'No reply': Amit Mishra reveals shocking cold shoulder from Virat Tilak has quietly become the batter India build their lower middle order around Pathan's point about versatility is the one worth holding onto, as it explains why India keep finding themselves rescued by the same player. Tilak has batted at three and four for India in the past, and on Saturday he came in at six behind a promoted Axar Patel and still produced the innings of the match. Very few batters absorb that kind of shuffling without their output dropping. The Dhoni comparisons are premature and probably unhelpful, since one 26-ball fifty does not build a finishing career. What is fair to say is that India have now won two completely different games in three days, chasing 226 and then recovering from 70 for 5, with Tilak central to the second of them. The concern it masks is that India's top order has been rescued rather than functioning. Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Shreyas Iyer contributed 52 runs between them, while Santner found enough in the surface to take four wickets on a ground where 181 should not have been difficult. India now lead 2-0 in the series, but a side that needs its number six to produce a miracle every time will not keep getting away with it. item.title: Infantino says backed by 'vast majority' in bid for re-election
item.description: Gianni Infantino believes his candidacy for re-election is backed by the "vast majority" of nations (Fabrice COFFRINI) FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old's hopes of winning a fourth term in charge. Infantino's future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football's world governing body to private investors. The heads of European football's governing body UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter saying football "belongs to no individual". But Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, is now in a strong position to secure re-election in March. "I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view," Infantino told the BBC on Saturday. "But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. "I'm just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I'm speaking to all associations everywhere in the world." No other candidate has yet come forward to oppose Infantino with the deadline to do so less than a month away on November 18. He added: "There are different points of view it's not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run." kca/ea

item.title: Raphinha makes huge claim about Lamine Yamal ahead of Ballon d’Or: ‘He’s the best player in the world’
item.description: Raphinha makes huge claim about Lamine Yamal ahead of Ballon d’Or: ‘He’s the best player in the world’ Barcelona are preparing to face Real Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou in the first El Clasico of the league season. Immediately after the game, the club will also await the results of the Ballon d’Or ceremony set to be held in London, with Lamine Yamal considered a favourite for the award. Ahead of the game, Raphinha has delivered a powerful endorsement of Lamine Yamal, insisting that his young team-mate is currently the best footballer in the world. The Brazilian also opened up about his struggles to reproduce his Barcelona performances with the national team. Raphinha believes Yamal is comfortably the world’s best Speaking in an interview on CazeTV , Raphinha praised Yamal’s exceptional quality and spoke about how much joy he brings to the sport. “Lamine is proving that he is the best player in the world right now, and I don’t think there is any room for debate about that,” Raphinha declared. “If you ask anyone who loves football, understands it and actually watches matches, they will realise how special he is.” Lamine Yamal is one of the very best players in the world. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The Brazilian went even further in his praise for the teenager. “For me, he is the best player in the world, perhaps by a very big margin over whoever is second.” Such praise coming from someone who is himself one of the best footballers in the world means a lot to Lamine. The teenager’s creativity, confidence and ability to decide matches have made him one of the team’s most important players under Hansi Flick. Raphinha’s comments also highlight the relationship and the mutual respect between the stars in the Barcelona attacking unit. Raphinha admits frustration over his Brazil performances The winger was equally candid when discussing the difference between his club and international performances. “I demand a lot from myself, and I know my results with the Brazilian national team are not the same as my results with Barcelona,” he admitted. “I’ve tried many times to find explanations and excuses for why I can’t perform at the same level with the national team.” He also revealed that injuries have disrupted his recent international involvement. “I recently suffered another minor injury, and I’ve had injury problems during the last three national team call-ups.” Raphinha opens up about his struggles with Brazil. (Photo by Ian Hitchcock/Getty Images) However, the Barcelona forward firmly rejected any suggestion that his difficulties stem from a lack of commitment. “I know my level with Brazil is far below what I produce at Barcelona, but it’s not because of a lack of care, desire or determination.” Raphinha’s self-criticism reflects the mentality that has helped him become such an influential player at club level. His willingness to acknowledge shortcomings, rather than hide behind excuses, is particularly encouraging. With El Clasico coming up

item.title: Confirmed lineups: 1. FC Köln vs Schalke
item.description: Confirmed lineups: 1. FC Köln vs Schalke Köln come into this game off the back of a 1-0 loss away at Frankfurt following a positive win in their last home match two weeks ago against rivals Borussia Mönchengladbach. For Schalke, it was a poor 1-0 defeat at home to Mainz which left the Ruhr side waiting for their first win at home this season. Köln will look to make it back-to-back home wins for the first time since January this year and to push up the table and improve on their 12th-place position. FC Köln (4-2-3-1): Schwäbe - Sebulonsen, Simpson Pusey, Lochosvili, Sosa - Krauss, Jóhannesson - Maina, Moore, El Mala - Bülter Schalke (3-4-2-1): Karius - Kuruçay, Katić, Becker - Gantenbein, El-Faouzi, Tanaka, Gosens - Dina Ebimbe, Aouchiche - Chan Hwang

FC Köln vs Schalke Köln come into this game off the back of a 1-0 loss away at Frankfurt following a positive win in their last home match two weeks ago against rivals Borussia Mönchengladbach. Köln will look to make it back-to-back home wins for the first time since January this year and to push up the table and improve on their 12th-place position. FC Köln (4-2-3-1): Schwäbe - Sebulonsen, Simpson Pusey, Lochosvili, Sosa - Krauss, Jóhannesson - Maina, Moore, El Mala - Bülter Schalke (3-4-2-1): Karius - Kuruçay, Katić, Becker - Gantenbein, El-Faouzi, Tanaka, Gosens - Dina Ebimbe, Aouchiche - Chan Hwang

item.description: After another lengthy roadtrip, your North Carolina Tar Heels return to Kenan Stadium for a primetime matchup. At 7:30 p.m. tonight, UNC hosts Syracuse in a battle of ACC football teams headed in opposite directions. North Carolina (4-2, 2-1 ACC) won each of its past two matchups, with fourth-quarter comebacks and late defense playing the greatest roles. The Tar Heels won back the Victory Bell last weekend , beating archrival Duke 24-20, their second-straight victory after winning at 25th-ranked Pitt on October 10. Syracuse (2-4, 0-2 ACC) entered 2026 with plentiful promise, returning a healthy Steve Angeli at quarterback and Fran Brown as head coach. The Orange started with a 66-3 obliteration of FCS New Hampshire, then lost four of its next five games, narrowly beating UConn by a 42-41 mark in overtime. UNC, on the other hand, entered this fall with plenty of question marks. North Carolina quickly answered those questions, showcasing a much-improved defense headlined by sophomores Xavier Lewis and Greg Smith . Billy Edwards looks much more comfortable running the Tar Heels' offense, which has three starter-caliber running backs in Benjamin Hall, Demon June and Jaylen McGill. Jordan Shipp is the WR1 North Carolina needs, while Jelani Thurman and Shamar Easter give UNC a big-play threat at tight end. The Tar Heels should win tonight easily, but they can't underestimate their opponent with three, one-score losses. North Carolina finally gets the night game it deserves on a cool, October night. item.title: NFL fumbles are climbing, and defenses are giving Peanut Tillman’s punch a bigger role
item.description: NFL fumbles are climbing, and defenses are giving Peanut Tillman’s punch a bigger role originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The ball is getting punched loose more often in the NFL, and the trend has made one old defensive technique feel new again. Through the first six weeks of the 2026 season, the league had recorded 235 fumbles, up 28 percent from the same point a year ago, according to Elias Sports Bureau data reported by the New York Post. That increase has brought extra attention to the “Peanut Punch,” the technique popularized by former NFL cornerback Charles Tillman: defenders strike at the football with a closed fist to force it free. Simplifying the idea The idea is simple. Tackling ends the play; punching at the ball can end the drive. But turning the move into a reliable part of a defense takes practice, timing and control. The NFL has sent teams video examples of legal punches as well as examples that can draw an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. 🤯 𝐖𝐎𝐖: NFL players have already fumbled the football 235 TIMES through the first six weeks of 2026. That's a 28% INCREASE from last season. Defenders are increasingly using the famous "Peanut Punch" technique to knock the ball loose. https://t.co/LJXOwx559t — Polymarket Football (@PolymarketBlitz) October 23, 2026 That creates a coaching challenge on both sides of the ball. Defenses want players to attack the ball when the opportunity is there. Offenses have to make sure ball carriers protect it through contact, especially when defenders are targeting the ball instead of wrapping up. Coaches have described ball security as a priority, with some teams giving it more practice time. MORE : Terry McLaurin injury leaves Commanders facing difficult wait after 49ers loss Where it started Tillman’s legacy is visible in that shift. His nickname became attached to a play that defensive coaches now teach across the league, years after he built a reputation for forcing fumbles in Chicago. The technique’s spread reflects the NFL’s constant search for turnovers, where even a small change in how a defender approaches a tackle can swing possession. The numbers do not prove that the Peanut Punch alone caused the increase. Fumbles can rise for many reasons, including game situations and individual mistakes. But the league’s emphasis on teaching the technique shows how seriously teams are taking the opportunity to create turnovers—and how much more urgently offenses must protect the ball. More NFL news: Joey Porter Jr. news considered ‘good’ after Steelers trade JJ McCarthy gets major starting job prediction despite New York’s 3-1 start Vikings get positive Justin Jefferson update after making wise decision against Dolphins

item.title: Lions vs. Packers 5 Qs preview: Unpacking Jordan Love’s volatile numbers
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers prepares to throw during an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off their early-season bye, the Detroit Lions pick up where they left off against their first NFC North opponent: the Green Bay Packers. We had the pleasure of connecting with Justis Mosqueda, the Team Community Producer for Acme Packing Company , to give us some insight into this Packers team ahead of this week’s matchup. We learned about Jordan Love’s wild mix of quick releases and deep shots amidst Green Bay’s pass-protection woes, the ongoing O-line carousel and Josh Jacobs’ potential impact on the run game, as well as Jonathan Gannon’s hyper-aggressive blitz scheme—plus much more. 1. Jordan Love’s numbers are the most fascinating thing to unpack with this Packers offense. He has the shortest time to throw in the NFL among 37 qualifying quarterbacks (2.48 seconds), yet he sports the sixth-highest average depth of target (9.5 yards) and according to Pro Football Focus, leads the league in big-time throws (15) and passing attempts of 20+ yards downfield (33). Through six weeks of the season, what’s the story of Love between these numbers? In short: Heroics. The offensive line performed poorly in the pass-protection game outside of Weeks 4 and 5. He has absolutely no running game to speak of. Love is taking a massive pounding week to week. It really is just the Kobe stan in Love coming out and willing the team to victory. The team also leads the NFL in drops over this time period, too, and a lot of those are on what would have been explosives and/or touchdowns. It’s incredibly frustrating to watch Love play at such a high level with the rest of the offense playing poorly around him. 2. Likely associated with Love’s performance this season is the offensive line and the running game. Injuries have thrown Green Bay’s offensive line into the centrifuge. Since the start of the season, they’ve acquired some familiar faces in Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler, and they’ve done their fair share of shuffling to figure out the best combination. Is this the week Zeitler makes his season debut? What’s your level of confidence in this line solidifying itself by the time these two teams meet again in January? item.content:encoded: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers prepares to throw during an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off their early-season bye, the Detroit Lions pick up where they left off against their first NFC North opponent: the Green Bay Packers. We had the pleasure of connecting with Justis Mosqueda, the Team Community Producer for Acme Packing Company , to give us some insight into this Packers team ahead of this week’s matchup. We learned about Jordan Love’s wild mix of quick releases and deep shots amidst Green Bay’s pass-protection woes, the ongoing O-line carousel and Josh Jacobs’ potential impact on the run game, as well as Jonathan Gannon’s hyper-aggressive blitz scheme—plus much more. 1. Jordan Love’s numbers are the most fascinating thing to unpack with this Packers offense. He has the shortest time to throw in the NFL among 37 qualifying quarterbacks (2.48 seconds), yet he sports the sixth-highest average depth of target (9.5 yards) and according to Pro Football Focus, leads the league in big-time throws (15) and passing attempts of 20+ yards downfield (33). Through six weeks of the season, what’s the story of Love between these numbers? In short: Heroics. The offensive line performed poorly in the pass-protection game outside of Weeks 4 and 5. He has absolutely no running game to speak of. Love is taking a massive pounding week to week. It really is just the Kobe stan in Love coming out and willing the team to victory. The team also leads the NFL in drops over this time period, too, and a lot of those are on what would have been explosives and/or touchdowns. It’s incredibly frustrating to watch Love play at such a high level with the rest of the offense playing poorly around him. 2. Likely associated with Love’s performance this season is the offensive line and the running game. Injuries have thrown Green Bay’s offensive line into the centrifuge. Since the start of the season, they’ve acquired some familiar faces in Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler, and they’ve done their fair share of shuffling to figure out the best combination. Is this the week Zeitler makes his season debut? What’s your level of confidence in this line solidifying itself by the time these two teams meet again in January? Meanwhile, the Packers have one of the worst rushing attacks in the league–but Josh Jacobs did come off the Commissioner’s Exempt List on Monday. How much do you anticipate Jacobs playing in this game based on Matt LaFleur’s comments this week, and do you think he’s the kind of difference maker who can single handedly get this run game out of the basement? I really think it could be. The running game has been bad all year, but at least Week 4 and 5 were games where the offensive line could at least protect Love. Last week, the Packers went into five-man protections for most of the game for the first time all season. This ended up exposing both guards a little more than anyone seemed to expect (Jacob Monk and Donovan Jennings started the year at guard before the team transitioned to Travis Glover and Laken Tomlinson). As of Thursday’s practice, the Packers were repping seven players to get ready for this game: the starting center (Sean Rhyan), the two tackles (Anthony Belton and Jordan Morgan) and four guard options (Glover, Tomlinson, Aaron Banks and Kevin Zeitler). I would not be shocked at all if we get Banks at left guard and Zeitler at right guard this week. If the Packers want to make that change before Week 9, they kind of have to do it now, because they have a short week against the Carolina Panthers after this. I 100 percent think Jacobs is going to play this week. LaFleur has really backed him at every opportunity to do so. The team has very much been in the business of getting Jacobs back on the field, even prior to the legal process playing out. They said he’s been working out with the team and in meetings the entire time. He just hasn’t been able to practice with them. They have three open roster spots on the 53-man roster that they’re keeping open right now, and two of those (Jacobs and PUP player Jordan Riley) are probably already filled in their minds. I think Jacobs can help turn some of those -2 runs into +2 runs, but I don’t think he’s just going to come into the lineup and fix all of Green Bay’s running game issues himself. 3. Former defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley left for a head coaching gig with the Miami Dolphins, and the Packers brought in Jonathan Gannon to replace him. What are some of the most notable differences you’ve noticed between the two coordinators, have said differences been mostly positive, negative or somewhere in between, and do you feel like the eventual return of Micah Parsons will end up making all the difference? The Hafley scheme was interesting, because it was mostly a scheme that disguised coverages, but didn’t do much on the pressure end, up until Micah Parsons came to town. When Parsons was on the field, teams obviously adjusted and ended up playing the Packers in more quick game and run game situations, which really forced Hafley to play more bland schemes—and Hafley went back to some “hidden” coverages once Parsons went down with an injury. Gannon’s defense really has been about bringing pressure. He’ll send seven guys on the first play of the game without blinking, and the cornerbacks have been playing pretty well this year (all three safeties have been great). They’ve done some interesting things with individual teams’ pass-blocking rules to get free rushers. It’s not uncommon for Gannon to scheme up a pressure where there are seven blockers on four rushers, one of the rushers is a free rusher, and the Packers still have seven coverage players for just three route-runners. The only time the defense hasn’t looked elite was against the Atlanta Falcons, which was a weird game. Bijan Robinson went crazy, and it seemed like everyone on both sides of the ball were slipping on the field that night other than Robinson. I think a lot of people are wondering if that was just a one-off or what the Packers’ defense looks like against a dynamic back. I think this week’s matchup will sort of answer that for us. Hopefully, Micah Parsons will be a big addition down the line, yes. Please, God. 4. Green Bay lost Edgerrin Cooper for the season after he suffered a torn Achilles in Week 4. Who has Gannon called on to replace Cooper, and how have the Packers adjusted on defense since the injury? Have you noticed any shifting in personnel groupings/deployment without their star linebacker available? EDITOR’S NOTE: This was asked and answered before Zaire Franklin suffered a mid-week injury and was declared out. The Packers use their linebackers a lot on special teams, because LaFleur’s offensive players hardly play teams—outside of the return positions. So they have Zaire Franklin at the Mike position (he doesn’t play teams) and now the Will role (previously Cooper) is being split by Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper. My guess is they’re rotating McDuffie and Hopper (they change every two series or so) so that they can keep their legs fresh on special teams. Behind them, Green Bay rosters two linebackers who are functionally special teams-only players in Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch, if you want to know how important those linebackers are for the Packers’ special teams unit. Last week, they also called up Arron Mosby (a hybrid edge-linebacker who is basically another full-time special teamer) against the Cowboys. Both McDuffie and Hopper have played well, but the linebackers have never really been tested (outside of the run game against Atlanta) this entire season. No one is really throwing over the middle against us, in part because we’re sending blitzers so much. It’s sort of hard to evaluate the position right now. In the moments when you would e

item.title: Chelsea announce multi-year sleeve partnership with payment firm Sokin
item.description: Chelsea announce multi-year sleeve partnership with payment firm Sokin Chelsea have announced a multi-year partnership with financial technology company Sokin, which will become a Principal Partner and the club’s Official Business Payments and foreign exchange partner. The sponsorship agreement covers both Chelsea’s men’s and women’s teams. Sokin’s logo will also appear on the sleeves of the home, away and third shirts for the senior sides and academy teams. The partnership brings together two London-based organisations with a global presence. Chelsea have millions of supporters worldwide, while Sokin provides financial services to businesses operating across international markets. The company’s platform handles more than $11 billion in business payments annually and serves organisations in over 170 countries. Sokin will help Chelsea manage the financial demands of operating across different currencies. The Blues work with international partners, compete in European and global competitions, and generate revenue from supporters and commercial activities around the world. Sokin provides businesses with payment services, multi-currency accounts, foreign exchange, checkout solutions and treasury management through a single platform. These services are designed to make international transactions easier while helping companies reduce the time and costs involved in managing payments through different banks and providers. As Chelsea’s official payments and foreign exchange partner, Sokin will support the club in sending, receiving and managing money across the currencies it uses in its daily operations. The company’s branding will appear on a Chelsea shirt for the first time when the men’s team host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea president Jason Gannon welcomed the agreement, explaining that the club looks for partners who share its ambition and willingness to embrace new ideas. “At Chelsea, we seek to partner with organisations that share our ambition and innovative mindset,” he said. “Sokin’s expertise in business payments, and their focus on making both simpler for the businesses they serve, makes them a natural fit for the club. “We are pleased to welcome Sokin to the Chelsea family and look forward to working together in the years ahead.”

item.title: Puka Nacua, DeVonta Smith, Christian Kirk and more WR injury updates for Week 7
item.description: Heading into the NFL weekend, all eyes are on wide receivers Puka Nacua , DeVonta Smith and Christian Kirk , as all three are uncertain to play in Week 7. Before we get to injury updates on those players, it’s worth noting that wideouts such as Rashee Rice, Emeka Egbuka, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel have been ruled out. On the opposite end of the spectrum, Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson have been removed from the injury report and are good to go. Here are the latest updates on Nacua, Smith, Kirk and other notable wide receivers who are uncertain to play. MORE: Fantasy football wide receiver rankings for Week 7 Puka Nacua injury update Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Nacua popped up on the injury report on Thursday and was limited with a calf issue he suffered in practice . He then followed that up with no practice on Friday before being listed as questionable to play. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport labeled the injury as “more minor than anything else,” but “not precautionary,” so that leaves some concern for his status. The Rams are walking a fine line because they need Nacua even more with Davante Adams sidelined , but they also can’t afford to lose Nacua for an extended period of time, which the Rams are running the risk of if they send him out there at less than 100%. Given the fact he didn’t return to practice on Friday, we’d say Nacua has a slightly worse than 50/50 chance to play. DeVonta Smith injury update Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) scores a touchdown during the second quarter at Nissan Stadium. Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Smith made his return last week, but he’s off to a bad start in Week 7 because his lingering hamstring injury has kept him out of practice on Thursday and Friday. The lack of practice over the first two days amounts to a downgrade in participation from last week, when he posted one limited and one full session. We’ll know more on Saturday, when the Eagles drop their final injury report. However, for now, Smith appears to be trending toward a questionable tag, at best. Christian Kirk injury update Houston Texans wide receiver Christian Kirk (13) celebrates a touchdown in the second quarter against the New England Patriots in an AFC Divisional Round game at Gillette Stadium. Credit: Brian Fluharty-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kirk appears set to make his 2026 and San Francisco 49ers debut this week after sitting out the first six contests due to a calf injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kirk turned in three full practices this week and is labeled as questionable to play. However, the expectation is he will be activated on Saturday in advance of playing on Sunday. Kirk could step into a big role immediately, as both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been ruled out. Dontayvion Wicks in

Credit: Brian Fluharty-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kirk appears set to make his 2026 and San Francisco 49ers debut this week after sitting out the first six contests due to a calf injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kirk turned in three full practices this week and is labeled as questionable to play. However, the expectation is he will be activated on Saturday in advance of playing on Sunday. Kirk could step into a big role immediately, as both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been ruled out. Dontayvion Wicks injury update Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (13) reacts after a reception during the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Like Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, who suffered an ankle injury in last week’s game, has not been able to practice over the first two days of the week. That is a bad sign for his chances of suiting up, but he’s got another crack at getting in at least some practice participation on Saturday. As of this moment, Wicks is probably headed toward a questionable tag, at best. Tank Dell injury update Houston Texans wide receiver Tank Dell (1) participates during the team’s minicamp at Houston Methodist Training Center. Credit: Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tank Dell appears set to make his long-awaited return to the field from the catastrophic knee injury he suffered in 2024. Dell practiced in full all three days this week before being given the questionable tag ahead of Sunday. Despite the questionable tag, Dell has been confirmed as good to go for Week 7. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: ‘In shock’ – Linda Cohn compares LeBron James’ golf swing during national anthem to a restless kid
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Former ESPN anchor Linda Cohn went off on LeBron James for not standing at attention during the U.S. National Anthem on opening night when the Philadelphia 76ers played the New York Knicks. Playing in his first game as a 76er, James appeared to be stretching his arms and shadow golfing while the national anthem was being played. A video circulating clearly shows that the player was constantly moving and after criticism from US President Donald Trump, even Linda Cohn went off on the 41-year-old. LeBron James criticised for moving like a restless child James’ video came to the spotlight just a day after the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream walked out before the national anthem during the WNBA Finals. Both teams have repeated this for three straight games and there has been a lot of criticism of the WNBA. Cohn questioned if the four-time NBA champion was jealous of the attention the WNBA was getting due to the controversy surrounding the national anthem. “People are standing in the sold-out crowd, and what is LeBron James doing? He’s acting like a three-year-old. He’s at the end of the line, the anthem is being played, and he’s practicing his golf swing. He’s doing a number of repetitions with his golf swing, and then he’s shooting air hoops, practicing his shot, a make-believe shot while the national anthem is going on. You know who does that? A three-year-old that can’t sit still… “I’m in shock. I mean, you don’t have to love LeBron. I admire him. He’ll go down in history as one of the greatest to ever play the game, but what is happening to him?” James has not directly responded to anyone about his behaviour during the national anthem but he did respond to what US President Donald Trump had to say to him. The 76ers have managed to win their first two games of the season with solid performances from James. Although he has been facing a few off-court issues, James has used his experience to put it all behind him and perform at an elite level when the game tips off. item.title: Broncos Trade Pitch Brings ‘Franchise Cornerstone’ to Offense
item.description: Indianapolis Colts offensive lineman Quenton Nelson. Getty Despite the praise heaped on the Denver Broncos‘ offensive line this offseason, the group has produced few results in its first six regular-season games. The Broncos may need a change — one that brings instant help and a different attitude. The Athletic’s Daniel Popper proposed the Broncos as a trade destination for Indianapolis Colts star guard Quenton Nelson, a move that would send longtime underachieving — and overpaid — guard Ben Powers to the bench. The NFL trade deadline is November 10. “Nelson is a franchise cornerstone in Indianapolis,” Popper wrote. “In his ninth year and age-30 season, he remains one of the best offensive linemen in football. Nelson is on an expiring contract, so the Colts would not have any dead money on their cap beyond this season if they trade their star left guard. The Colts could get immediate draft capital for the 2027 draft. If they hold on to Nelson and let him walk in free agency, any potential compensatory pick would not materialize until 2028.” For the Broncos, that equation might be as simple as offering a conditional 2027 3rd-round pick that becomes a 2nd-round pick if Nelson starts more than one playoff game. Quenton Nelson: Dominant Player on Terrible Teams Nelson, 6-foot-5 and 330 pounds, was the Colts’ No. 6 overall pick out of Notre Dame in the 2018 NFL Draft and, like everyone else in the Colts organization, has been left reeling since star quarterback Andrew Luck shocked the football world with his retirement right before the 2019 season. Since then, Nelson has mostly dominated whoever is unlucky enough to line up across from him on some pretty terrible teams — the Colts have made the playoffs just once and haven’t won a playoff game since Luck retired. Don’t feel too bad for Nelson, a 6-time NFL All-Pro and 8-time Pro Bowler — he will have banked an incredible $118.3 million in career earnings through the end of the 2026 season. Ben Powers Reworked Contract in Offseason In July, Powers agreed to restructure the 4-year, $52 million contract he signed before the 2023 season after struggling with injuries in 2025. In 2026, he’s struggled with his performance. According to Pro Football Focus, Powers’ 52.8 overall grade ranks him 56th out of 76 eligible players at his position. “Sources told 9NEWS the Broncos’ starting left guard accepted a restructured, one-year contract that will leave him with less pay but more of it guaranteed,” 9News Denver’s Mike Klis wrote . “A source said while the pay cut was significant, Powers will be still be drawing ‘starter’ money in 2026. Powers had been scheduled to earn $13 million this season, although none of it was guaranteed until he made the season-opening, 53-man roster. Now, it’s a training-camp battle between Powers, a natural left guard, and Alex Palczewski , a natural right tackle who filled in nicely at left guard for Powers last season. item.title: Wisconsin needs more out of transfer running back Abu Sama vs. USC
item.description: As long as Luke Fickell is at the helm of the Wisconsin Badgers , the offense will want to be run by an elite quarterback. In Fickell’s most successful seasons with the Cincinnati Bearcats , the offense was led by quarterback Desmond Ridder, who compiled 115 touchdowns in his heroic career. This year, the Badgers have been led by quarterback Colton Joseph , and thus far, Joseph’s play has been wildly inconsistent, which means the Badgers need to get star running back Abu Sama III more time on the ball. Sama was injured in Wisconsin’s 24-20 come-from-behind win against Penn State, and he returned last weekend against UCLA but only had six carries for 34 yards. So far this season, Sama has totaled 224 yards on the ground with an average of 6.6 per carry and 56 per game, along with one touchdown this season. Sama has only had one game this year with double-digit carries. It's also worth noting that in his most impressive game of the year against Western Illinois, when he finished with 107 yards, 102 of those came on his first two carries. So far this season, the Badgers rank No. 97 in rush attempts per game at 32.8 and will be going up against the No. 29 rush defense in the country, the Trojans , who allow just 111 yards per game. While Sama may struggle to churn out meaningful runs against a stout defense, the Badgers need to take pressure off Joseph if they want to keep the ball away from a dangerous USC offense. item.title: Australian umpire's Ranji Trophy sojourn: Aeroplanes overhead at Palam, BKC's red soil pitch, love for garlic naan and vada pav
item.description: NEW DELHI: Last week, when umpire Ben Treloar stepped out to officiate the Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Gujarat at the Palam Air Force II Ground, he caught everyone's attention. Players from both sides were curious about the Australian umpire, with most approaching him on the opening day of the drawn fixture, in which Delhi secured the first-innings lead, to ask where he was from. "Quite a few players asked me where I was from and what was going on. They were genuinely welcoming and interested," Treloar told TimesofIndia.com from Mumbai. The 44-year-old from Sydney is in India for the first time as part of the Umpire Exchange Program for the 2026-27 season between Cricket Australia and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). As part of the programme, Australian umpire Ben Treloar will officiate in two Ranji Trophy matches in India, while Indian umpire Parashar Joshi will travel to Australia to stand in two Sheffield Shield matches and one One-Day Cup fixture. "It's my first time in India, and I'm really enjoying the experience. Everything is brand new, and I'm experiencing it for the first time. At the end of the day, it's just another game of cricket, but one of the differences is that I don't know any of the players here, and they don't know me. We're all meeting for the first time. "The similarity is the high standard of cricket. The players are incredibly talented, and the standard of first-class cricket here is very high. It's similar in Australia [in the Sheffield Shield], where we also have gifted players who perform at their best," he says. "The other similarity is the passion with which the game is played. Players here and back in Australia play for their livelihoods. They play hard, play fair and compete in the right spirit. It's great to be out in the middle, be part of that and contribute to the game. "The playing conditions are slightly different, particularly the session timings. The first session here lasts two and a half hours because play starts a little earlier, whereas in Australia, the first session is two hours before the lunch break. The number of overs is also different. Here, it's 90 overs a day, compared to 96 in Australia," he adds. For Treloar, who has been umpiring for the past 21 years, the most unique experience at Palam was the aeroplanes frequently flying over the ground. "Palam was great. It's obviously a smaller venue, and there isn't as much infrastructure around the ground. There were aeroplanes flying overhead, probably one every five minutes across the four days. item.content:encoded: NEW DELHI: Last week, when umpire Ben Treloar stepped out to officiate the Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Gujarat at the Palam Air Force II Ground, he caught everyone's attention. Players from both sides were curious about the Australian umpire, with most approaching him on the opening day of the drawn fixture, in which Delhi secured the first-innings lead, to ask where he was from. "Quite a few players asked me where I was from and what was going on. They were genuinely welcoming and interested," Treloar told TimesofIndia.com from Mumbai. The 44-year-old from Sydney is in India for the first time as part of the Umpire Exchange Program for the 2026-27 season between Cricket Australia and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). As part of the programme, Australian umpire Ben Treloar will officiate in two Ranji Trophy matches in India, while Indian umpire Parashar Joshi will travel to Australia to stand in two Sheffield Shield matches and one One-Day Cup fixture. "It's my first time in India, and I'm really enjoying the experience. Everything is brand new, and I'm experiencing it for the first time. At the end of the day, it's just another game of cricket, but one of the differences is that I don't know any of the players here, and they don't know me. We're all meeting for the first time. "The similarity is the high standard of cricket. The players are incredibly talented, and the standard of first-class cricket here is very high. It's similar in Australia [in the Sheffield Shield], where we also have gifted players who perform at their best," he says. "The other similarity is the passion with which the game is played. Players here and back in Australia play for their livelihoods. They play hard, play fair and compete in the right spirit. It's great to be out in the middle, be part of that and contribute to the game. "The playing conditions are slightly different, particularly the session timings. The first session here lasts two and a half hours because play starts a little earlier, whereas in Australia, the first session is two hours before the lunch break. The number of overs is also different. Here, it's 90 overs a day, compared to 96 in Australia," he adds. For Treloar, who has been umpiring for the past 21 years, the most unique experience at Palam was the aeroplanes frequently flying over the ground. "Palam was great. It's obviously a smaller venue, and there isn't as much infrastructure around the ground. There were aeroplanes flying overhead, probably one every five minutes across the four days. By the end of the match, you sometimes don't even realise a plane is coming because you get used to it," he says. "But that doesn't change what we do out in the middle. It's another ground, another first-class match and another opportunity to officiate some really good cricket. What I noticed was how passionate everyone involved in the match was about cricket and providing excellent hospitality. From the caterers and ground staff to the players, team management and coaches, everyone was welcoming and made it a really good experience," he adds. Away from the field, Treloar works as Cricket New South Wales' Umpire Education Officer, helping develop the next generation of match officials. His contribution to umpire education has been recognised with four George Borwick Memorial Awards from the New South Wales Cricket Umpires and Scorers Association. "I'm very grateful to both the BCCI and Cricket Australia for maintaining such a strong and positive relationship. The way they support match officials and provide them with these additional experiences is fantastic. We're very thankful for the opportunity, and I was honoured and proud to be offered the chance to come to India," he says. He will next umpire the third-round match between Mumbai and Haryana at Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) ground. "I've had a quick look at the BKC ground in Mumbai, and it's a much more established venue. I'm really looking forward to getting out there in a couple of days and experiencing a different type of pitch. This one has red soil, so I anticipate it will offer a little more. We'll also spend some time watching the nets and getting a feel for the conditions before the match," he says of the BKC pitch. Apart from cricket and the contrasting soil types (black soil in Delhi and red soil in Mumbai), Treloar has been enjoying Indian cuisine and its flavours. He is also noting down recipes to take back home for his family. "The food has been incredible. It's spicy, I must tell you. I do ask for mild food, but I've really embraced the cuisine in both Delhi and Mumbai. The food has been high quality, with so much flavour, and I'm really enjoying it. "I particularly like the stuffed potatoes. I've been eating a lot of vegetarian food, and the dal, the quality of the breads, including roti and garlic butter naan, and the vegetable curries and vada pav have all been fantastic. "When I get home, I'm looking forward to expanding my cooking abilities. I'll be cooking a lot more of these dishes for my family," he says. 135165996

item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
item.description: Head coach in hospital after collapsing in training Assistant coach Aaron Danks to take charge against Freiburg Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. Continue reading...

item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, José Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...
